#1865. GdS: ‘Milan choose their next star’ – Cardinale prepares €70m for the January window

AC Milan proved that they are willing to spend money on talent in the summer and in January, it’ll seemingly be no different.

There was a shift in the works at Milan in the summer. No longer were the club going to focus solely on buying quantity over quality, hoping for a gem. Instead, they were going to buy quality and so far, it’s largely paying off.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Now, the roadmap is there to do the same again in a few months.

According to Gazzetta dello Sport, as seen below, Cardinale is ready to invest around €70 million. After the €150m spent in the summer, it represents a substantial season of investment from the American and it seems this will be the trend moving forward.

There are currently decisions being made about who arrives, but it seems more likely that a new striker will be chosen and there are two standout names for the Rossoneri; both aren’t unfamiliar, too.

On one hand, you have Endrick and the other, you have Nicolo Tresoldi.

Starting with the former, the relationship between Roc Nation and Cardinale is strong, which could help negotiations. Of course, the American was also very keen to sign him in the summer mercato, so this interest stretches back.

They will have to compete with Roma, but to help give them the upper hand, they have involved Kaka in the process. The Brazilian – also an evangelical Christian – could do with Endrick ‘what Leonardo did with him’.

Cardinale plans to offer a loan with a buy clause to help sweeten the deal, and this could be worth €60m, plus bonuses. Importantly, he’d also be willing to offer Real Madrid a buy-back clause, similar to the Nico Paz situation.

With Tresoldi, things aren’t as simple. Their admiration is well known – as is the striker’s for the Diavolo – but they are not alone in their interest. His future lies away from Belgium, but the path is difficult to know.

Ideally, they wouldn’t sell him in January, but if a compelling offer arrives, he could well leave the club in the New Year. It may also be problematic if Premier League clubs become involved; they are desperate to avoid an auction.

#1864. When is Nations League draw? Start time, confirmed pot numbers and TV channel for quarter-finals

The 2026-27 Nations League draw for the quarter-finals takes place this week, as the business end of the competition comes into focus.

England are among the five teams to have qualified for the knockout phase, as things currently stand, with Thomas Tuchel’s side enjoying a near perfect group phase.

Their only defeat came against reigning world champions Spain on matchday one in September, though the Three Lions exacted revenge on Sunday night as they held on after being reduced to 10-men to seal a famous victory.

As a result, England topped Group A3 at Spain’s expense due to a superior goal difference and that means they are likely to avoid another European heavyweight in the quarter-finals.

Elsewhere, France sealed top spot in Group A1 with a 2-1 win over Turkey, while Belgium thumped Italy 4-1 to finish as runners-up.

In A2, Germany topped the table with a 5-0 thrashing of the Netherlands, who slipped to second on goal difference after such a swing.

Portugal’s position in Group A4 is still to be confirmed after they were humbled at home by Denmark in their first game since Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football.

The Nations League draw for the 2026/27 quarter-finals will take place on Friday, November 20, following the conclusion of the group phase fixtures.

As well as the quarter-final draw, the promotion/relegation play-offs draw will also be conducted.

Coverage of the draw is due to start at 11am GMT, with the draw itself expected to begin shortly afterwards.

The Nations League draw will take place in Nyon, Switzerland.

TV channel: In the UK, the draw will be televised live UEFA TV.

Live stream: You can also stream the draw for free online via the UEFA YouTube page.

Live blog: You can follow the draw as it happens on the day through Standard Sport’s live blog.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

The group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - will be kept apart.

The four group winners will be seeded in Pot 1, with the four runners-up will be unseeded in Pot 2.

*Portugal are guaranteed a Nations League quarter-final spot, though can still finish first or second in Group A4.

#1863. Real Madrid transfer news: Fabrizio Romano reveals truth behind Trent Alexander-Arnold to Liverpool links

By Saikat Mandal | 15 Nov 2026 20:31

Trent Alexander-Arnold has struggled to secure regular game time at Real Madrid this season, but a return to Liverpool in January appears to be out of the question.

The 28-year-old joined Madrid from Liverpool in the summer of 2025 and has made 43 appearances for the Spanish giants across all competitions.

However, the England international has managed just four starts in La Liga this season, with a further three appearances coming off the bench.

Alexander-Arnold has lost his place to Federico Valverde, with Jose Mourinho preferring to deploy the midfielder at right-back ahead of two recognised full-backs.

This has fuelled speculation that a potential return to Liverpool could be on the cards, but Fabrizio Romano has poured cold water on those rumours.

Romano has dismissed suggestions that all three parties are involved in discussions over a potential transfer.

Alexander-Arnold rose through Liverpool's academy to establish himself as one of the best right-backs in world football, although his departure from Anfield was not universally well received.

"Let’s immediately clarify one thing, there is zero ongoing between Trent Alexander-Arnold, Real Madrid and Liverpool, zero at all," said Romano to DAZN Football, as relayed by Roundtable.

The Italian journalist further emphasised that, while Alexander-Arnold retains enormous affection for the Reds, his priorities remain firmly in the Spanish capital.

"Trent obviously respects and loves the club but that’s it, it’s in the past. Trent is fully focused on Real Madrid and there is no contact or negotiation at all with Liverpool."

The England right-back would have been a fantastic addition to Andoni Iraola's system, but it appears unlikely that the Reds have any plans to bring him back.

Jeremie Frimpong has struggled to make a significant impact, but Ronald Araujo, who joined on loan from Barcelona, has done a decent job at right-back so far.

Conor Bradley remains sidelined through injury and is unlikely to return before the end of the year, but bringing in another right-back is not currently a top priority for Liverpool.

#1862. Libya vs Tunisia - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 15 Nov 2026 21:42

Tunisia will be looking to repair their faltering Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign when they travel to the 11 June Stadium in Tripoli to face Libya on Tuesday.

The Mediterranean Knights moved onto four points from three Group H matches with Friday's victory in Sfax, while the Eagles of Carthage sit bottom of the table with two points, still waiting for their first win of the campaign.

Libya opened their AFCON qualifying campaign with a 2-2 draw at home to Botswana, coming from two goals down through Marwan Al-Habashi's strike in the 87th minute and Ezoo El Mariamy's penalty deep into stoppage time.

They then suffered a 1-0 defeat away to Uganda, with Arnold Vula scoring the only goal, leaving them bottom of Group H before Friday's result moved them towards the top end of the table.

Coach Youssouph Dabo, the Senegalese who replaced Ali Cisse, had not won a competitive match in charge before Friday, making the victory all the more significant.

In Sfax, Libya took the lead after Ali Maaloul fouled Muaid Issa in the box, allowing Ali Youssef to convert from the penalty spot in the 44th minute, before Hamdou El Houni doubled their advantage on the counter-attack shortly after the hour mark.

The result marked Tunisia's heaviest home defeat in AFCON qualifying and the first time they had trailed by two goals on home soil in the competition.

It also ended more than 25 years without a two-goal home defeat in the qualifiers, prompting angry supporters to throw bottles and set off flares, while players and staff confronted referee Hamza El Fariq, who was subsequently escorted from the stadium.

Coach Mouine Chaabani has since apologised to supporters and admitted that the defeat was deserved, although Tunisia's decline stretches further back than the current qualifying campaign.

They lost all three matches at the 2026 World Cup, suffering defeats against Sweden (5-1), Japan (4-0) and the Netherlands (3-1), and have now gone nine games without a win, including September's draws against Uganda (1-1) and Botswana (2-2).

Before this campaign, Tunisia had qualified for each of the last 17 AFCON finals, the longest active streak of any nation, but with only one team besides co-hosts Uganda able to progress from Group H, they are running out of room for error.

Their record against Libya remains encouraging, however, as the visitors had won the previous six meetings before Friday's encounter, including a 5-2 away victory in 2021 and 3-0 and 1-0 wins in 2023.

Tunisia Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Libya are expected to rely heavily on home-based players from clubs in Tripoli and Benghazi, with Youssouph Dabo naming a 27-man squad for the double-header.

Al Hilal Benghazi forward Ezoo El Mariamy is among the main attacking options, while Hamdou El Houni will be hoping to recover from the injury that forced him off during the first leg after scoring.

Tunisia have also named a 27-man squad built around experienced internationals Ferjani Sassi, Aissa Laidouni, Ali Maaloul and Montassar Talbi, while Moetez Zemzemi and Mohamed Ali Ben Hammouda are among the new additions.

Elias Achouri was ruled out through injury before the first leg and has not been included in the squad for the trip to Libya.

Tunisia desperately need a victory, but they have scored just three goals in three qualifiers while conceding five, and Libya showed how dangerous they can be on the counter-attack in Sfax, with another positive result likely to leave the hosts in a strong position.

The visitors should be more assertive away from the pressure of their own supporters and possess greater individual quality, but their recent struggles suggest they could again enjoy plenty of possession without creating enough clear-cut opportunities.

Mauro Biello is confident that Canada can "do really good things" after they qualified for the CONCACAF Nations League Finals with a 4-1 victory over Guatemala on Monday.

Canada took a 3-2 lead into the second leg at BMO Field but were without Alphonso Davies, who suffered a muscular issue in the opening match and joined the likes of Cyle Larin, Stephen Eustaquio and Ismael Kone on the injury list.

Despite a strong start from the hosts, Oscar Santis drew Guatemala level on aggregate when he showed great composure on the edge of the six-yard box in the 34th minute.

But Jonathan David equalised from the spot five minutes later and Tani Oluwaseyi made it two on the stroke of half-time, putting Canada back in control of the tie.

Tajon Buchanan scored his first international goal since last year's Gold Cup after the restart and Oluwaseyi nodded in his second before the hour mark to complete a 7-3 aggregate victory.

Biello, who stood in for the suspended head coach Jesse Marsch, suggested Canada's injury problems could help spur them to a first trophy since winning the 2000 Gold Cup by increasing the competition in the squad.

"These are tough games. It was a tough game also in Guatemala, and you saw it here: you're in total control of the game, and then it's 1-0 to them," said Biello.

"Getting these injuries is not fun. You're losing key guys, but at the same time, we're expanding this pool of players.

#1859. Niger vs Morocco - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 15 Nov 2026 21:42

Niger will be looking to respond to their heavy defeat in the first meeting when they face Morocco again in Tuesday's 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying fixture at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat.

The Mena suffered a 5-1 defeat in Casablanca on Friday, leaving them with three points from three Group A matches, while the Atlas Lions maintained their perfect start to the campaign and moved onto nine points after winning all three of their qualifiers.

Niger began their qualifying campaign with a 2-1 victory over Lesotho, but they were unable to build on that result when they travelled to face Gabon, suffering a 2-0 defeat in their second Group A fixture.

They then lost by the same scoreline to Algeria in an international friendly in October, before Friday's 5-1 defeat against Morocco extended their losing run to three matches across all competitions.

Their latest defeat was particularly frustrating because they managed to reduce the deficit to 2-1 before half-time through Mohamed Abdouramane's header, and were handed an opportunity to equalise shortly afterwards when a penalty was awarded for a handball by Noussair Mazraoui.

However, Yassine Bounou saved Ousseini Badamassi's spot kick, and Achraf Hakimi restored Morocco's two-goal advantage with a free kick in first-half stoppage time before the Atlas Lions added two more goals after the break.

The Mena have now conceded nine goals in their last three outings, including a 2-1 friendly defeat to Algeria, while scoring just twice during that period, leaving coach Nabil Neghiz with plenty to address after a difficult start to his tenure.

Morocco have now scored nine goals and conceded just once in their opening three qualifiers, having started the campaign with consecutive 2-0 victories over Gabon and Lesotho before Friday's emphatic win.

The Atlas Lions also drew 1-1 with Mali in a friendly in October, but their competitive form has been considerably more impressive, with the latest result extending their winning run in AFCON qualifying to nine matches.

Morocco have also won their last 16 home matches in major tournament qualifiers, covering both the Africa Cup of Nations and World Cup, marking their longest-ever winning streak on home soil in such fixtures.

With Tuesday's match also taking place in Morocco, with Rabat serving as Niger's adopted home for this fixture, Mohamed Ouahbi's side will remain on familiar territory and look to make further use of that advantage.

Morocco have consequently won the last three encounters between the sides by an aggregate score of 12-2 and boast a perfect record in this fixture, having won all seven meetings across all competitions.

Niger Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Morocco Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Niger named a 25-man squad for the November double-header, with nine players based in the domestic league and the rest drawn from clubs in Europe, Asia and other African countries.

Rahim Alhassane, who plays for Bologna, is expected to remain an important figure in defence, while Oumar Sako, Ali Mohamed, Daniel Sosah and experienced winger Tidjani Amadou Moutari are among the other notable selections.

Morocco are also working with the 26-man squad named by Ouahbi for the two matches, although several established internationals are missing, including Ismael Saibari, Azzedine Ounahi, Ayoub El Kaabi, Soufiane Rahimi, Chadi Riad and Hamza Igamane.

Youssef En-Nesyri returned to the squad and scored after coming off the bench in the first meeting, while Ayoub Oufkir marked his first senior call-up with a late goal, with both forwards now hoping to earn starting places after their contributions in Casablanca.

#1857. Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG

Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

Emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the big positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

Signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the new year.

Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj

His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

Doué forced a save from Marco Bizot and, after Villa failed to clear, the loose ball landed in the path of Kvaratskhelia, who cut inside on the left to his right foot before smashing a shot into the roof of the net.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx

It was a strike of sheer power and accuracy, catching Bizot by surprise. PSG briefly appeared in control, but Villa responded superbly. In 17 minutes they created six goal-scoring chances before the outstanding Madjo finally made one of them count.

Before his goal, he had narrowly missed the target twice with a pair of headers from John McGinn’s crosses. Villa also had another opportunity 10 minutes before half-time, when Pacho’s mistake allowed Hemmings to run from the centre circle unopposed. As he entered the penalty area, the PSG defenders had raced back to recover and a promising moment ended with Madjo curling a shot wide.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15

PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov then produced his first save just before the break, turning away Boubacar Kamara’s close-range header. Villa did carve out another golden chance when Madjo’s strength took hm past Pacho, but he hit the outside of the post. Madjo’s moment did come, though, as he once again bullied Pacho to divert a McGinn cross into the roof of the net.

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr

Villa were buoyant, but it was PSG who scored the crucial second goal after Doué was awarded the goal following a VAR review. Doué was sent clear down the right by substitute Ousmane Dembélé and confidently beat Bizot, with reviews concluding that he had been played onside by Matty Cash.

The game was refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but was denied entry to the United States.

It became rather fractious as time began to tick away, with McGinn booked after complaining over the placement of a free-kick. Madjo was replaced by Tammy Abraham with 17 minutes left and this will be an evening he will never forget.

PSG (4-3-3): Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Mendes (Hernandez 75), Neves (Ruiz 75), Vitinha, Emery, Akliouche, (Dembele 45), Doue (Mayulu 87), Kvaratskhelia (Buraldo 88).Substitutes: Chevalier (g), Zabarnyi, Digne, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.Villa (4-2-3-1): Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres (Mings 80), Maatsen, Kamara (Bogarde 72), Gomes (Barkley 79), McGinn 7 (Alysson 73), Buendia, Hemmings, Madjo (Abraham 72).Substitutes: Wright (g), Asemota (g), Barkley, Nedeljkovic, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.Booked: Gomes, Torres, McGinn.Referee: Omar Artan (Somalia).

After the officials and the Aston Villa players receive their medals, it is time for the 2026 Uefa Super Cup winners PSG to receive their medals. The last man up is their captain Marquinhos, who has won a staggering 40 trophies during his time at PSG. He takes the trophy from Uefa President Aleksander Ceferin and lifts it above his head alongside his teammates.

PSG are your 2026 UEFA Super Cup Champions 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/1qCKEQ0IPK

Both Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have been heavily linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and neither player came off the bench for PSG tonight. Does that indicate that potentially those moves could be close, with neither played risked of picking up an injury?

Luis Enrique has now won 13 trophies with PSG. Serial winner 🏆 pic.twitter.com/RAsyI1Ui2s

💬 "We are ALWAYS hungry you know... we want more, we want more" Désiré Doué reflects on PSG's UEFA Super Cup Final win.📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nwreU1Skz7

Aston Villa will take on Borussia Mönchengladbach on Saturday in their final game of pre-season before they take on Brighton on the south coast on the opening weekend of the new Premier League season.

PSG play Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before they kick off the defence of their Ligue 1 crown at home against Rennes.

Buendia has a late chance to equalise for Aston Villa from Maatsen’s cross but his header goes wide.

Not long after, the final whistle goes and PSG win the Super Cup for the second straight year. Last year they beat Tottenham on penalties, this time they beat Aston Villa 2-1. Unai Emery’s side acquitted themselves well and will regret some of their missed chances tonight. An entertaining affair in Salzburg.

PSG win back-to-back UEFA Super Cup's following goals from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vzMx6rGjuo

Dembele feeds a pass into the Villa box looking to pick out the run of Hakimi but there is slightly too much on it and Bizot is out to gather.

Into the final minute of added time we go.

Aston Villa are running out of time to find a late equaliser.

Maatsen brings Dembele down not far outside the Aston Villa box but play goes on as the latter gets up and shoots, with his effort saved by Bizot.

One final change for PSG as their other goalscorer tonight, Kvaratskhelia, is replaced by Beraldo. A defender comes on for an attacker as Luis Enrique’s side look to hold on for the victory.

Mayulu is coming on for Doue, whose goal may well have won back-to-back Super Cups for PSG.

The ball falls to Kvaratskhelia on the right side of the box and the Georgian chips it over Bizot but Cash is on hand to clear. Aston Villa then counter and Abraham feeds a pass forward at the perfect time to pick out the run of Alysson into the PSG box. Alysson then plays it across the six-yard box but neither Abraham nor Maatsen are there to meet the cross.

Double change for Aston Villa as Barkley and Mings replace Gomes and Torres, who were both on yellow cards.

Alysson, only just on the pitch, does brilliantly down Aston Villa’s right and drives into the PSG penalty area. His cross is parried away by Safonov straight into the path of Gomes, whose shot is blocked by Zaire-Emery.

PSG are making a double substitution as Ruiz and L Hernandez come on. Neves and Mendes, who had been struggling with cramp, go off.

Aston Villa are going to make a triple change as Abraham, Alysson and Bogarde come on. 17-year-old Madjo is one of those to be replaced as is McGinn, who has been booked as he goes off. The Aston Villa captain is distinctly unimpressed with the officials.

The space opens up for Mendes to take on the shot from range and he obliges, forcing Bizot into a decent save. Kvaratskhelia is unable to make contact with the follow-up. Mendes seems to be struggling with some cramp.

We are nearly 70 minutes into the game but Unai Emery has still not turned to his bench yet.

Aston Villa have an immediate chance to equalise through Hemmings but the 19-year-old’s effort from inside the box is straight at Safonov. That was a big chance for Hemmings.

Down the other end, Gomes is booked for a challenge from behind on Doue.

The VAR has checked it and there was no offside so the original decision is overturned and the goal is given. Doue is played in behind by Dembele down the right channel and is played onside by Cash on the far side. Doue takes it into the Villa penalty area and gets it onto his left foot. He curls it past Bizot and into the far corner.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj

Doue has the ball in the Aston Villa net but the offside flag has gone up. However, has Cash played Doue onside?

Cash’s cross from the right picks out Buendia at the front post but the latter’s header is off target. Unai Emery will be pretty happy with his side’s performance through the hour mark.

Mendes is a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul on McGinn as the Aston Villa captain spun the Portuguese defender on halfway. The referee must have thought both players had a hold of each other but I would lean towards Mendes probably fouling McGinn.

Other than 10/15 minutes in and around Kvaratskhelia’s goal, Aston Villa have put in a good performance and have created more chances than PSG. If anything, it will be Villa who will be disappointed that they have not scored more than once.

Just inside the PSG penalty area, McGinn cuts onto his left to get his shot away and his deflected effort is saved by Safonov diving to his right.

One of Aston Villa’s coaches has been booked for some protestations after Torres is penalised for a foul on Doue. Torres is also booked for that challenge.

Two of Aston Villa’s best players tonight thus far have been teenagers; 19-year-old Hemmings and 17-year-old Madjo. Aston Villa have seen some key, senior players depart this summer but will take joy from the performances of this pair.

Luis Enrique has decided he needed to make a change at the break as Dembele replaces Akliouche, who was quiet on his official debut for PSG after his move from Monaco.

Incredible to think he is only 17 years and 212 days old. He’s been all over PSG centre-back Willian Pacho and thoroughly deserves his goal.

The teenager could even have had a hat-trick. What a second-half this could be.

Madjo has managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s Georgian magician Kvicha Kvaratskhelia, which is quite some achievement.

Possession: PSG 67%-33% Aston VillaShots: 6-10Shots on target: 2-2Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 11-17

After one added minute, the first half is brought to an end and we are all square at 1-1 in Salzburg. Kvaratskhelia had put PSG in front but Madjo’s goal on the stroke of half-time has Aston Villa level at the break.

On the stroke of half-time, the 17-year-old levels for Aston Villa and finally takes his fourth big chance of the night. It is perhaps the hardest chance he has had as McGinn’s cross comes all the way to the back post. Madjo is being held by Pacho but somehow gets his foot to it and his shot goes into the roof of the net. What a moment for the 17-year-old!

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr

Madjo has his third massive chance of this first half and this shot comes off the post. Buendia feeds a pass forward into the path of Madjo, who appeared to be blocked by Pacho but he outmuscles him. Madjo then fires towards goal but it strikes the outside of the post. In a parallel universe, Madjo could have ahd a first-half hat-trick.

Aston Villa have had a few great chances in this first half and there is another. A free-kick into the PSG penalty area causes issues for the French side and Kamara’s header towards goal is saved by Safonov.

Madjo has his second huge chance of this first half. Once more it is McGinn who provides the cross. The Scot does really well on the right side of the box to fake the cross with his left and instead delivers with his right. He picks out Madjo at the back post and the 17-year-old should score but his header misses the target. What a story it would have been had the 17-year-old scored two goals against the Champions League winners.

Aston Villa have just settled things down. Either side of Kvaratskhelia’s goal, they were on the ropes but have calmed things down.

Hemmings is played in and he could potentially have gone down twice under challenges from Hakimi and then Mendes. The ball then falls to 17-year-old Madjo on the left side of the box. He opens up his body and tries to curl into the far corner but his effort goes wide.

Referees are now hot on players taking too long over throw-ins, with Mendes falling foul of that. That is one of the fairly new rules that will be good for the game.

A huge chance for 17-year-old Madjo to equalise. McGinn picks out the young striker with a sublime cross from the right. Madjo is just eight yards out and has a free header but it goes just wide of the far post. Aston Villa should be level.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15

After Aston Villa had made a solid start to this game, it is all PSG right now and Villa are on the ropes at the moment. PSG work it beautifully down their left after a sublime one-two between Mendes and Kvaratskhelia. Mendes drives down the left wing and has a cross into the box first-time which he declines. The Portuguese defender then has four different teammates that he could pick out in the penalty area but his cross misses all four.

PSG want a penalty. Kvaratskhelia shows great feet out on the left to drive into the Aston Villa penalty area. Gomes is on his back and Kvaratskhelia goes down. It did look like he was always looking to go down and it would have been very soft.

A few minutes after I said that Aston Villa had done a decent job of keeping PSG at bay, Luis Enrique’s side take the lead. Bizot had just made a great reflex save to deny Doue but he is unable to stop Kvaratskhelia’s effort. The Georgian cuts inside onto his right just inside the Aston Villa penalty area and gets his shot away quickly after quick feet. There is great venom on the shot and it beats Bizot, who thought Kvaratskhelia was going to go for the far corner but instead hit it at the near post. Could Bizot have saved that? Perhaps but Kvaratskhelia did belt that shot.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx

As you would expect, PSG are dominating possession but thus far have been unable to create any genuine chances, much to Aston Villa’s credit. But, with the players PSG have at their disposal, they can cause chaos in a moment.

Tensions just start to simmer. McGinn gives a foul away on Mendes, who then attempts to take the free-kick a good few yards further forward from where it was. McGinn repeatedly tries to stop Mendes from taking it further forward before the referee steps in to end the dispute.

Moments later, Kamara decides to shoot from range and his low, driving effort goes wide of Safonov’s right post. With Onana injured long-term and Tielemans now at Manchester United, Kamara’s importance to Aston Villa is even higher.

In last year’s Super Cup, PSG were stunned in the first hour against Tottenham as went 2-0 down before coming back to win on penalties. PSG have played fewer friendlies than Aston Villa up until this point so there may be a little more rustiness in Luis Enrique’s side than Unai Emery’s.

This is going to be a very tall order for Aston Villa, who look very different tonight to how they ended last season, up against a team of PSG’s calibre. Not only have Villa sold some key players like Rogers and Tielemans but the likes of Konsa and Watkins are yet to return after the World Cup.

McGinn is afforded too much space and time to cut onto his left foot out on the right and whip a dangerous cross towards the far post. Pacho is on hand to head away with a great defensive header.

Moments later, good work from Maatsen out on the left earns Aston Villa a corner. Unai Emery’s side have made a decent start to this game. Buendia’s delivery into the near post is headed away by Marquinhos.

We are under way in Salzburg, where it has been a very hot day but the temperature has cooled a touch with the sun having set in Austria.

Some huge banners are on display on the pitch, displaying not only the emblems of the two clubs but also images of the trophy lifts that have earned these sides a place in tonight’s game. Both sides emerge from the tunnel, past the trophies they won with the two captains carrying them out, and we are moments away from kick-off in Salzburg. Here is a reminder of how the sides line up tonight:

💬 " I am confident they're going to play today with the level we need" Unai Emery on the inclusion of João Gomes and Brian Madjo into Aston Villa's lineup. 📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/FCjBmGDcNo

Lucas Digne has only just swapped Aston Villa for PSG in recent days but he already comes up against his old teammates. He is on the bench for PSG tonight and could offer some good insight into Unai Emery’s side.

PSG forwards Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and both are on the bench for PSG tonight. As PSG close in on moves for Ferran Torres and Mika Godts, could Liverpool’s moves for Barcola and Mbaye accelerate in the next few days? Barcola has only recently returned to training after the World Cup and is joined on the bench by compatriot Ousmane Dembele. Maghnes Akliouche, who has joined PSG from Monaco this summer, starts tonight.

Brian Madjo is just 17-years-old but he starts up top for Aston Villa tonight against the Champions League winners, with Ollie Watkins yet to return after the World Cup.

“There is a lot of change but when you look at other clubs in England, there is a lot of change. What we have still is our main core, same manager, same methods and same desire to achieve more. New Villa signing Alejandro Garnacho has been ruled out tonight as part of the concussion protocols.

Garnacho was signed from Chelsea last month and took a whack to his face in the recent game against BG Pathum in Thailand.

Tonight’s game will be refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but got turned away at the border.

Team news is in 🔒 #PSGAVL pic.twitter.com/yeKkyIKiHQ

What will we learn from the “new Aston Villa” tonight? After the sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, this is a Villa team in transition.

Unai Emery virtually admitted last night it could be another slow start to the season, like last year. Villa face a full-strength PSG team hoping to win the Super Cup for the second time in a row.

I don’t think we can take much from this result tonight, whatever it is. Villa cannot be properly judged until the window closes. Don’t bother telling that to Unai Emery, though. He is ready to continue defying the doubters.

The Champions League and Europa League winners fight it out in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg as PSG take on Aston Villa. PSG took on English opposition in the Super Cup a year ago, when they played Tottenham. PSG fell 2-0 down in that game in Udine but scored two late goals to take it to penalties, where they won 4-3. These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. The two clubs have been involved in a transfer this week, with left-back Lucas Digne re-joining PSG from Aston Villa.

Aston Villa have played in the Super Cup once before back in 1982 when they took in Barcelona. They lost the first leg 1-0 over at Camp Nou but fought back to win the second leg 3-0 at Villa Park to claim the trophy. Aston Villa were last in action out in the Far East last Friday, falling to a 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich in Hong Kong. It has been a big summer of change at the club, with key starters like Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans departing and the likes of Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Gomes arriving.

“I feel like the club is in a new era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”

Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

“I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

“No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”

PSG have added Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche and Digne to their ranks this summer. They are also pushing to sign Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Mika Godts from Ajax. Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool but have been included in their squad for tonight’s game, as have Akliouche and Digne.

#1856. Arsenal: Declan Rice agrees new long-term contract as Gunners target period of dominance

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Declan Rice has agreed a new long-term contract with Arsenal.

The midfielder began talks with the club over improved terms earlier in the year and those have accelerated in recent weeks.

It is understood that a verbal agreement has now been reached and Rice will soon put pen to paper on the deal.

The long-term extension will see Rice receive a huge pay rise, taking him up to bracket of Bukayo Saka as the club’s best-paid player on around £350,000-a-week.

Rice has established himself as a central figure in Mikel Arteta’s side ever since he arrived for £105million from West Ham in 2023.

The 27-year-old secured his first piece of silverware for the Gunners last season, winning the Premier League in a campaign in which he played 69 matches for club and country.

Rice’s previous deal was set to expire in 2028 but both parties have been relaxed about the situation, even after he entered the final two years of that contract.

The England international made it clear that he wanted to stay at Arsenal, while the club never had any intention of losing him.

Rice follows Arteta in committing his future to the club. Bukayo Saka, William Saliba and Gabriel are among those to have also signed new long-term contracts.

Arsenal are keen to tie down the core of their first-team squad as they target a period of dominance over the next few years.

Discussions have been ongoing with Jurrien Timber, who like Rice would have been out of contract in 2028.

Those talks are also believed to be nearing a conclusion after an agreement was improved on an improved contract for the Dutchman.

By Ben Knapton | 15 Nov 2026 21:48, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 22:02

England inflicted Spain's first defeat in 43 games on the World Cup winners with a sensational 3-2 victory in the Nations League, thus progressing to the quarter-finals as group winners.

Evidently learning their lessons from their gut-wrenching World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina, the Three Lions exploded out of the blocks in the Spanish capital, but Luis de la Fuente's backline weathered the early storm.

The world champions soon began to threaten James Trafford's goal too, but England got the reward their endeavours warranted on the stroke of the break, as Harry Kane dispatched a controversial penalty.

Neither the home nor away fans could then comprehend what they witnessed inside the opening 15 minutes of the second half, as Arsenal duo Ezri Konsa and Ben White incredibly extended England's lead, but the visitors were then forced to strap in for a nail-biting ending.

Barely moments after England's third went in, Elliot Anderson was sent off for a last-man foul and Mikel Oyarzabal dispatched the resulting penalty, before an Anthony Gordon error ended with Nico Williams cutting the arrears further.

However, the 10 men of England heroically held out in the dying embers to condemn Spain to their first loss since March 2024, and usurp the world and European champions at the top of League A Group 3.

#1854. Prediction: Bayern Munich vs Koln

Marking their return from November’s international break on Friday night, Bayern Munich will welcome Koln to the Allianz.

With the rest of Europe’s elite domestic leagues making their respective returns this weekend, there are plenty of eye-catching betting promotions available.

Ahead of Friday’s Bundesliga battle, you can find all of the key Bayern Munich vs Koln H2H stats here.

Starting with the hosts, welcoming back Vincent Kompany to the touchline this weekend, Bayern Munich will be excited to make a return from November’s fortnight interval. Last seen heading into the final international break of 2026 with a 2-1 victory away at Mainz, it is no secret that the German giants are universally regarded as the standout contender to once again defend their Bundesliga crown this season. Marking their return sat at the top of the table, Bayern will be looking to make another public statement here. Getting their Champions League adventure underway with a real flurry and yet to suffer a single competitive defeat across all competitions so far this season, Kompany’s superstar squad have also gained a fearsome reputation for their free-scoring performances in the final third. In fact, the former Burnley boss has seen his squad notch 29 goals in their first nine Bundesliga appearances.

Along with welcoming Kompany back to the Allianz dugout this weekend, German international Jamal Musiala is also expected to make a first Bundesliga appearance since the middle of September. However, suffering from a muscle injury prior to November’s international break, former Liverpool star Luis Diaz remains on the sidelines.

Crowned as the new Ballon d’Or winner during an emotional ceremony in London last month, talismanic number nine Harry Kane will lead the line in Munich. Registering nine direct goal contributions in as many Bundesliga appearances this season (six goals, three assists), Michael Olise will partner Kane in the final third.

As for the visitors, while Koln might have eventually maintained their Bundesliga status last season, the Billy Goats appear destined for another relegation scrap this time around. Marking their respective return from November’s international break holding just a two-point buffer over the drop zone, Rene Wagner’s side couldn’t have asked for a tougher examination when they travel to Munich this weekend. Last seen heading into the fortnight interval with a 2-1 defeat at home against Bayer Leverkusen, Koln have mustered just a sole win from any of their previous eight Bundesliga appearances. Along with failing to find any kind of clinical edge in the final third, Friday’s guests will be concerned by a nightmare record against Bayern. Including a 5-1 drumming when they last travelled to the Allianz back on May 16th, they have lost each of their last six straight battles by an aggregate score of 19-4.

Yet to make a maiden Bundesliga appearance this season, German midfielder Timo Hubers remains on the sidelines with a serious knee injury. However, Wagner’s side could welcome back one-time Sparta Rotterdam youngster Ragnar Ache for the first time since the start of October.

While Tottenham loanee Mikey Moore might still be waiting to open his Bundesliga account, the England U21 international will feature in Munich. Bagging what turned out to be a consolation strike against Bayer Leverkusen last time out and featuring for Germany over the past fortnight, 20-year-old Said El Mala will lead the line on Friday night.

Excited to welcome Kompany back to the Allianz dugout on Friday night, Bayern Munich will be confident of laying down another domestic marker. Marking their return from November’s fortnight interval once again leading the chase at the top of the Bundesliga standings, the reigning German champions have yet to suffer a single defeat across any competition since opening the new campaign. Cruising their way to a routine 5-1 victory when they last welcomed Koln to the Allianz back in May, Bayern hold a dominant record against Friday’s guests. Winning their previous six consecutive Bundesliga battles by an aggregate score of 14-4, a free-scoring Bayern will be confident of putting on a show.

#1853. Who will England face in Nations League quarter-final? Next opponents confirmed after Spain win

England are on course to record their best ever performance in the Nations League, having qualified for the quarter-finals as group winners ahead of world champions Spain.

Including its inaugural season in 2018/19, the Three Lions have competed in every single Nations League campaign, experiencing some highs and the lowest of lows.

From topping their group and qualifying for the Nations League finals and finishing third to suffering a shock relegation in 2022/23 and then immediate promotion, England have done almost everything except win the competition.

Having started the 2026/27 campaign with a loss to Spain, despite leading 2-1 at one stage, England bounced back in style by beating the Czechs twice and then thumping Croatia 7-0 in a remarkable, record-breaking rout.

Another win over Croatia followed at Wembley to confirm a top-two finish in the group and qualify for the Nations League knockout stage.

England then beat Spain in a one-game shootout in Madrid to win the group and with that, potentially securing, an easier quarter-final tie next March.

The four group winners will face the four runners-up in a two-legged Nations League quarter-final.

The group winners will all be seeded and will have home advantage in their respective second leg ties. Teams from the same group cannot be paired together in the knockout stage, therefore England and Spain - for example - will be kept apart.

As a result of finishing top in Group A3, England’s confirmed potential Nations League quarter-final opponent are Belgium and the Netherlands after they were pipped to top spot in Group A1 and A2 by France and Germany respectively.

England’s remaining possible quarter-final opponents will be revealed on Tuesday night, but as things currently stand, they could be drawn against either Portugal, Denmark or Norway.

The draw for the 2026/27 Nations League quarter-final will take place on Friday, November 20 with the ties scheduled to take place in March 2027.

#1852. Maldini admits career could’ve been different without father and Liedholm: “Liked playing goalkeeper”

Things could’ve been much different for Paolo Maldini at AC Milan without two major figures in his life and career.

Maldini has two faces at Milan, but both remain adored by the fanbase. Firstly, you have the legendary defender, whose number was retired with him, a sign of respect and a chance to honour a career and legacy which surpasses many in the game.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Then, he returned as the sporting director, ending the Scudetto drought. Of course, that story didn’t have an ending as romantic as his playing career, but his legacy lives on. In fact, he may be voted into the Hall of Fame in the very near future.

Speaking to Tuttomercatoweb, via PianetaMilan, Maldini looked at the earliest stages of his career, as well as when he really took off for the Rossoneri.

“When my father took me to try out for AC Milan, I liked playing goalkeeper, but luckily I ended up choosing to be a defender. I played football with my friends in the park and at the youth club: I didn’t feel like I was destined for success at all, and until the day I made my debut, I never thought I could reach the highest levels.

“My dad always told me that the most important thing is to have fun, because if you treat it only as a job, it loses its magic.”

“There’s one person in particular who believed in me and wanted me to play when I was 15: Nils Liedholm, then AC Milan’s coach. He loved showing his faith in young players, and once, during a break, he asked me whether I preferred to play on the right or left. I replied that it was obviously his choice, but it was a gesture that helped me a lot.”

As they say, one change and the rest is history. With Maldini, that was certainly the case.

#1851. Mauricio Pochettino reveals Manchester United U-turn after Pep Guardiola talks

Mauricio Pochettino says he has a point to prove at Manchester United, after revealing his conversation with Pep Guardiola prior to sealing a return to club management.

The Argentine was appointed new Man United head coach last week, succeeding Michael Carrick who was sacked as a result of a disappointing start to the season with the side languishing in the Premier League relegation zone.

This will be the 54-year-old’s first job in club management since leaving Chelsea at the end of the 2023-24 season and fourth overall in England’s top-flight following spells at Southampton and Tottenham.

Despite the announcement, Pochettino does not officially start work at Man Utd until Wednesday as he has been granted permission to finish up with the United States Men’s National Team [USMNT] before reporting to Carrington.

6-0 up from the first-leg of the CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final against Haiti, it is expected to be a routine exercise for USA in the early hours of Wednesday morning [UK time] for what is Pochettino’s farewell game.

Speaking with the Telegraph in preparation of saying goodbye to international management, Pochettino said he admitted to Guardiola in September that he missed the day-to-day element of club management.

“I am ready [to return],” he said. “This is what I miss a little bit. I miss to be, every day, with something here.

“Guardiola asked me when I was at the game, he said, ‘Oh, you don’t want to come back to the Premier League?’ I said, ‘No, I’m happy here.’

“[He said] ‘Yeah, but you don’t miss, every day, to…’ I say, ‘A little bit, yes, because you think now today, and then we have December camp against Jamaica for the MLS [players in the pool].

“But after, you need to wait [until] March. What do you do? You need to watch games, you need to travel – administrative things. That is nice, it’s good.

“But every day, to be involved: press conference, training, everything … this type of possibility, like with United, you say yes. I want that. I want to prove myself again.”

#1850. Tanzania vs Nigeria - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 15 Nov 2026 21:57, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 22:05

Africa Cup of Nations co-hosts Tanzania will be seeking their first win of the qualifiers when they welcome Nigeria to the Amaan Stadium on Tuesday.

While the match carries little significance for the hosts - already assured of a place at next year’s finals - the visitors remain fully focused, as a win would all but secure their own qualification.

No team in AFCON history has recorded more podium finishes (17) than Nigeria, who are regulars at the competition. After wins over Madagascar and Tanzania, either side of a 3-0 defeat to Guinea Bissau, the West Africans are on course to reach the tournament finals once again.

Despite missing several key attacking players, Eric Chelle’s men scored three goals in a competitive match for the first time since January, hinting at attacking depth across the squad, which is crucial given their overreliance on Victor Osimhen at times.

The Super Eagles have topped their AFCON qualifying group in each of the last four campaigns but currently trail Guinea Bissau by three points, so they cannot afford further slip-ups if they hope to finish as group winners.

Winless in their last four outings (D2, L2), Tuesday's visitors have been underwhelming away from home lately, so supporters travelling to Zanzibar City will be wary of further disappointment, with September’s heavy defeat in Bissau still fresh in the memory.

Converting just 10% of their chances so far, Nigeria need a much sharper edge in front of goal, especially given their ongoing defensive woes, having now gone six matches without a clean sheet since a 3-0 win over Jamaica in May.

While the result was inconsequential in the grand scheme, Tanzania were largely competitive in the first half of their 3-1 defeat to Nigeria, but a lacklustre second-half display set the stage for a second defeat in three outings.

Miguel Angel Gamondi’s men would have hoped the AFCON qualifiers might provide a preview of what to expect on their fifth appearance at the competition next year. However, based on recent results, hopes of a fairytale showing on home soil are quickly diminishing.

The Taifa Stars have now won just one of their last 16 matches across all competitions - a run that includes two meetings with Nigeria, who are unbeaten in seven previous encounters, winning five.

Tanzania are still awaiting their first competitive home victory since being awarded a 3-0 win over Congo in March 2025. As a result, some sections of the nation's faithful will approach this clash hoping for the best but expecting the worst.

A good start would help settle any nerves, but Tuesday’s hosts have conceded first in five of their last seven outings, and a repeat of that would be catastrophic, to say the least, given their current dry patch.

Ademola Lookman and Victor Osimhen are both ruled out with knee injuries, after Lookman was forced off just before half-time on Friday.

Igoh Ogbu (Achilles) and Samuel Chukwueze (thigh) are also unavailable for the visitors, who continue to monitor the fitness of Frank Onyeka.

Tolu Arokodare came off the bench to score twice last time out and could be rewarded with a start here as he looks to continue his impressive run of form.

Ibrahim Hamad is Tanzania’s most notable absentee due to a knock, following an impressive display at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium.

This should open the door for Charles M’Mombwa to come into the hosts’ starting XI, although Evastus Lukanima could also be considered.

#1848. Pochettino would tell Guardiola to take USA job

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Mauricio Pochettino would tell Pep Guardiola to take the job as the United States head coach if he is offered the chance.

Despite signing a new four-year contract with the USA after leading them to the World Cup quarter-finals in July, Pochettino last week agreed to take over at Manchester United following the dismissal of Michael Carrick.

Guardiola is reportedly US Soccer's favoured candidate to replace Pochettino having left Manchester City at the end of last season.

Asked what he would tell Guardiola if the USA made an official approach, Pochettino replied: "Take it.

"Why? Because it’s a perfect moment to arrive at the federation. Everything is on the right path, in the right direction. Of course, take it.

"Of course, you are going to find really good players, good people – the players can fit his style."

Six goals on Saturday to set ourselves on the front foot. ROLL THE HIGHLIGHTS! https://t.co/J6y6JrEuzv

Pochettino was seen as a coup for USA when he took over and he now believes the role has evolved into one of the most desirable jobs in football.

#1845. Liverpool transfer news: Billionaire owner 'obsessed' with signing Virgil van Dijk for free as FSG contract decision nears

By Lewis Nolan | 15 Nov 2026 23:18

AC Milan owner Gerry Cardinale is obsessed with the idea of signing Liverpool defender Virgil van Dijk, the latest report has revealed.

The Reds' centre-back has so far enjoyed a strong season in England, helping the Merseysiders keep four clean sheets in their first 10 Premier League games.

However, fans are worried about the Dutchman's future given his contract is set to expire at the end of the campaign.

The 35-year-old has hinted that he would like to stay at Anfield, but there has seemingly been little movement regarding an extension.

Italian outlet Gazzetta dello Sport now claim that AC Milan's majority shareholder Cardinale is obsessed with the idea of signing Van Dijk.

Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG) have implemented a policy focused on rewarding younger stars at the club, while also moving on experienced players before they decline beyond the point of use.

There have been exceptions to those rules, with Van Dijk and Mohamed Salah both signing deals in 2025 following impressive seasons.

However, Salah struggled considerably in 2025-26 before leaving for free in the summer transfer window, and it would be understandable if the club were reluctant about handing another deal to a player in the twilight of their career.

Van Dijk's performances may be deserving of a contract offer, but FSG are unlikely to be swayed by any sentiment shared by fans, and they will instead make an emotionless judgement call in 2027.

Van Dijk is still one of the most physically imposing defenders in Europe, with the centre-back having won 75% of his duels in the Premier League this season.

Losing his experience would place significant pressure on Jeremy Jacquet next term, and the 21-year-old would benefit from spending more time without being the main man at the back for Andoni Iraola.

Liverpool are also likely to lose Alisson Becker and Joe Gomez for free in the summer, so ensuring there is someone at the club that has been through the peaks and troughs of life at Anfield would be sensible.

The Dutchman has been hampered by injury issues during his time at Arsenal but when fit has been consistently trusted by Mikel Arteta.

Speaking after the Netherlands were beaten 5-0 by Germany on Monday night, shortly after reports of a contract agreement broke, Timber effectively confirmed that new was correct.

“Those are good reports,” Timber said. “They are definitely on the right track. It will all work out, yes.”

In addition to that, Raya is also expected to sign a new deal with the club.

The Spaniard has established himself as one of the best goalkeepers in the world and last week was named in the 2026 FIFPRO World 11.

Raya became only the second Arsenal player to make that team, 20 years on from Thierry Henry being included in 2006.

The 31-year-old was handed an improved salary last year, though that adjustment to his contract did not extend the length of the deal.

Raya is now close to finalising a new long-term contract that will keep him in north London into his mid-30s.

It is an emphatic response to recent discussions on Raya potentially eyeing a move to Spain at the end of his current contract.

Speaking to Marca last month, Raya said: “I would love to play in La Liga one day. Right now, I’m very happy at Arsenal. But it’s true that I’d love to play in LaLiga one day. It’s a very competitive league.

“I’m Spanish and I’d love to play in Spain, that’s obvious.”

Arteta, though, has been adamant that he wants Raya to remain at Arsenal in the seasons ahead.

“I think David has to play in Spain at some point… on the beach, with his friends in the summer,” Arteta said in response to Raya’s interview.

“But for the next few years he needs to play here for Arsenal.”

Arteta looks set to get his wish, with Raya joining Rice and Timber in ensuring he spends the prime years of his career at Arsenal.

#1843. Nicaragua vs Montserrat - prediction, team news, lineups

By Saikat Mandal | 15 Nov 2026 23:27

Nicaragua and Montserrat will face off in the second leg of their CONCACAF Nations League play-in tie at the Nicaragua National Football Stadium in the early hours of Wednesday morning UK time.

The Blue and White claimed a 2-1 victory away from home in the first leg and will head into the return fixture full of confidence as they look to finish the job in front of their home supporters.

Juan Cruz Real's side have endured a horror Nations League campaign, failing to pick up a single point from four matches.

They have scored only four goals and conceded 14 as they finished at the bottom of League A's Group A.

After four defeats in a row, Nicaragua produced a strong performance at Estadio Cibao, where they took full advantage of an extra man after the home side were reduced to 10 men inside the opening 20 minutes.

Despite going a goal down, an own goal from Samuel Fenton sparked a revival, while Efrain Mejia scored in the 72nd minute to give them a slender lead heading into the second leg.

Montserrat are the underdogs in this tie, having earned their place in the play-in round from League C, but they have shown few weaknesses so far.

Despite losing a man so early in the first leg, they still managed to find the net, meaning the tie remains very much in the balance heading into the return fixture.

Gabriel Calderon's side won all four of their matches in League C's Group A, scoring 11 goals and conceding just once.

Montserrat kept clean sheets in three of those outings, but they have never tasted victory against their opponents in four attempts, which could prove a psychological hurdle.

Nicaragua could look to field a similar side to the one that started the first leg, although Cruz Real may be tempted to hand right-winger Mejia a starting role after his impressive performance earlier this week.

Juan Barrera failed to make a significant impact in the previous match, but he is still likely to retain his place, with Jaime Moreno once again expected to make a cameo appearance from the bench.

The visitors will definitely be without Lenni Cirino, who was sent off in the first leg.

Captain Alex Dyer appeared to pick up an injury towards the closing stages of that encounter before being replaced by Vashim Roache, and his absence would represent a major blow.

Tyrone Baker may have to settle for a place on the bench, but versatile midfielder Kaleem Simon could come into the starting XI.

Mayorga; Gutierrez, Cano, Perez, Quijano; R Cole, Salinas, Hernandez, Mejia, Talavera; Smith

Carter-Rodgers; Cirino, Furlong, Dorsett, Townsend-West; Barzey, Kirnon, Dyer, Simon; Comley, Boatswain

Nicaragua have failed to keep a clean sheet in their last six matches and have conceded the opening goal in five of those encounters. However, buoyed by their first-leg victory, we expect the hosts to produce a stronger performance on home soil and narrowly secure another win.

#1841. Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end

Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

It was a shame because in that cameo, Fernandes showed he has returned from the World Cup in excellent shape, the tempo of United’s play immediately lifting when he had the ball. It is wrong to make conclusions in the summer, but you are on safe ground to state he will be integral to their ambitions.

Croke Park is a stadium steeped in history and another chapter was penned here, as the capacity crowd made this the highest attended soccer match in Ireland with 82,000 coming through the gates: it is a magnificent venue, one that would be well capable of hosting a Champions League final.

Michael Carrick hopes in years to come that is the stage where his team will be but, right now, it is a case of learning to walk again before they can run and he more than anyone will know how far off that target is, not that it will stop him trying to get there.

The one thing that is obvious about the way United play under him is the first thought from everyone is to go forward quickly. Yes, this was only a friendly, but the ambition to be on the front foot and cause problems was evident from the start.

The team in red had much the better of the opening exchanges, with Diogo Dalot having the first shot that went over but, unlike on July 25, when Mayo beat Kerry here in Gaelic football’s All Ireland final, which went viral, nobody was cheering the sight of a ball clearing the bar.

It was like a home game for United and the majority got what they wanted in the 15th minute when a slick counter-attack ended with Bryan Mbuemo sliding a pass into Joshua Zikzee, who rifled past James Trafford with a first-time finish.

Devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n

Zirkzee is unlikely to be part of Carrick’s squad beyond the transfer window, with interest from clubs in Italy, and it would be disingenuous to suggest his career at Old Trafford has been successful, but his attitude was exemplary and he played as if he was desperate to change his manager’s mind.

There may have been an anticipation that United would stride clear, but this game was also about Leeds, whose summer has been encouraging and whose confidence from staying up last season has evidently enabled them to blossom.

You would be way off the mark if you include them in your conversations about which clubs are going to be relegated next May, and the sense they showed to stay with Daniel Farke has paid off. They have bought some good players, not least goalkeeper James Trafford and Harry Wilson.

Top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA

Trafford has done the right thing getting away from Manchester City and you could argue that he is already reaping the benefit of playing for a manager who wants him, as he made a fabulous save in the 23rd minute to thwart Mbuemo. It was all part of performance that led to him being named player of the match.

He was involved in the move that brought the Leeds equaliser, too, as his long clearance caused uncertainty and led to Tyler Fletcher being pickpocketed by Dan James and he nudged a pass into Brenden Aaronson, who kept his cool and danced into the area, ignoring Senne Lammens, to finish.

Leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6

It was an entertaining affair, mercifully lacking the bile that would usually bubble away when it is staged in England, and the longer the game advanced, the better Leeds looked. They finished the opening period strongly and came back after the restart, with 10 changes, in the same fettle.

Farke, whose team had shown their ability to score heavily when they pummelled Liverpool 4-2 in Chicago 10 days ago, would have taken plenty of encouragement, but the perfectionist in him would have cursed the opportunities that were squandered early in the second period.

The misses proved costly as the game meandered and the shoot-out went United’s way, after Wilson and James Justin failed from 12 yards, with Noussair Mazraoui thumping in the decisive kick. It really is never dull.

Manchester United Lammens (Mee 61); Dalot (Mazraoui 60), Yoro, Heaven (Armer 46), Amass (Shaw 60); Santos (Collyer 46), T Fletcher (Tielemans 61); Diallo (J Fletcher 60), Zirkzee (Cunha 60), Dorgu (Thompson 46); Mbuemo (Fernandes 60).Subs not used Heath, Honor, Lacey, Gabriel.
