Decent enough watch for roughly half the game, settled on a shoot-out in which Alex Cairns got nowhere near any of Manchester United’s penalties. Doubt he will lose much sleep over it. Bruno Fernandes grinned broadly when he missed.

Bottom left. Manchester United win the Boyle Sports Cup.

Smacks it even higher into the top right.

And I think Amapdu’s signal means Leeds will go first.

The ref decides to call time as the stewards cannot catch the juvenile intruders.

Not sure what we can say about stadium safety here but the game has ended prematurely after five kids came on, all of whom got to Bruno Fernandes to take selfies. It was very funny but, equally, plenty on the Manchester United bench were far from happy. Penalties to follow.

Some sealion ball juggling from Mazraoui involving foot, thigh and head, gets him past Justin on the right  but Gnonto heads away his cross.

Two young Man Utd fans run on to the pitch to try to take selfies with Man utd players. They are joined by three more and now another.

Bruno Fernandes lets fly from 20 yards, cushioning a pass from Tielemans before hammering his shot into the crossbar with little backlift.

Gnonto breaks down the right, plays it infield to Wilson who runs at the heart of the Man Utd defence but smacks his shot into a defender.

Cresswell blocks Mazroui’s shot with his right elbow which was pinned to his side and the ball falls to Bruno Fernandes but Cresswell is there again to block the shot, this time with his legs. From the corner, Bruno Fernandes balloons a long shot over the bar.

Enormous frustration for the masses who have wanted a Bruno goal. He’s just “scored” - right on the moment when our friend the stadium announcer bellowed the match was a sell out but never provided the actual figure – but a linesman’s flag has stopped him in his tracks. You fancy he will have one more involvement before the game creeps towards a penalty shootout.

Bruno Fernandes shoots past Cairns with a left-foot shot from 16 yards, smacking it inside the left post but the flag had long been raised.

The ball pinballs out to Justin by the D from the corner and he hammers a shot that Mee saves with great agility by the right post.

Excellent pass from Okafor from the left ought to have put Calvert-Lewin through but Armer does brilliantly to hold him up. Gnonto makes a run down the side but Calvert-Lewin checks back to shoot into Armer and the ball deflects behind for a corner.

There will be a shootout if the match is drawn after 90 minutes. The Boyle Sports Cup cannot be shared, it seems.

Mazraoui drives down the right and feeds it inside to Fletcher whose deflected cross falls kindly for Thompson but the young striker cannot control it and Leeds recover.

Amapdu hurls a long throw into the box on the diagonal from the right. Rodon flicks it on and Calvert-Lewin dives to try to nod it past Mee but he can only stick his effort wide. It was just a bit too far in front of him to reach with control and power.

Clever pass from Gnonto sends Wilson into the box on the underlap to cross low, seeking Calvert-Lewin. Mee is out to stop it reaching him. Oakfor sets off on a  bustling run down the left for 35 yards but then fluffs the cross.

Jack Fletcher is playing on the right with Tielemans and Collyer as the central two. Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha are playing centrally with Thompson on the left. Nothing much happening as Leeds keep their defensive shape while Manchester United probe away.

Yoro and Bornauw are the only two starters left. Stach intercepts Matheus Cunha’s cross in from the right.

Understandably Manchester United look disjointed now. Leeds have had longer for their changes to settle.

Seven Manchester United changes: Mee, Tielmans, Shaw, Bruno Fernandes, Jack Fletcher, Matheus Cunha and Mazraoui incoming for Dalot, Lammens, Amass, Mbeumo, Diallo, Zirkzee and Tyler Fletcher.

Dalot slides in to trip Okafor after the Swiss forward was played through the middle by Calvert-Lewin. Stach takes the free-kick from 22 yards, bends it round the wall but Lammens read it well and steps across to catch by the right post.

Zirkzee’s trickery down the right leaves Justin in his wake but having done the hard bit he fluffs the cross, delivering it too high for a shot and too low for a header. Thompson tries to contort himself to reach it but no one is that flexible.

Couple of threatening crosses from Gnonto from the right just elude Calvert-Lewin and Alfie Cresswell, son of Richard, brother of Charlie, follows up the second to shoot from the edge of the box. Lammens gathers comfortably.

Just the 10 half-time changes for Leeds and the worst thing about that was the fact it gave the stadium announcer, who hadn’t grasped that he didn’t need to shout into a loud speaker system, the opportunity to screech unchecked for close to two minutes, leaving everyone with tinnitus. Give the wrong man a microphone and chaos will ensue. Anyway, we are underway in the second period and the one change the majority of the stadium wants to be see is the introduction of Bruno Fernandes. His presence would help United regain some impetus.

Huge cheer as Bruno Fernandes, Luke Shaw et al start to warm up.

Lammens saves from Harry Wilson’s shot from 10 yards after Rodon’s underlapping ran down the right caught Amass off guard.

Senne Lammens to the rescue! 🧤A great reaction save from the Belgian 👏🇧🇪 pic.twitter.com/GRau9yk02n

Thompson tackles Rodon as he tried to lengthen his stride down the right.

Oddly Bornauw, who is poised to join Hamburg on loan, is the only player kept on from the first half for Leeds.

Gnonto, who is playing at right wing-back, is palyed down the line by Rodon and bends over a low cross looking for Calvert-Lewin’s late run. Lammens dives out to smother it.

Manchester United make three changes – Tynan Thompson, Toby Collyer and Dan Armer replace Santos, Heaven and Dorgu.

Cairns; Rodon, Bornauw, Cresswell; Justin, Ampadu, Stach, Gnonto; Wilson, Okafor; Calvert-Lewin.

Pleasant summer watch between largely second string players. Mbeumo looks a class apart from the other attacking players. On this evidence he might be worth a punt for goals and assists topping 25 this season like they did in 2024-25 for Brentford. Though he may have to take pens off Bruno Fernandes to get there.

The ref blows directly on 45 minutes moments after Nmecha rab out of room to control Tanaka’s cross and booted it out for a Man Utd goal-kick.

Manchester United probe patiently for half a minute around the Leeds area but the pass supposed to play Mbeumo through is picked off by Bijol and he plays it out to James who hares off down the left for 50 yards, cuts in on his right after leaving Yoro in his vapour trail, and whacks a shot over the bar from 22 yards.

Yoro hooks Bogle’s long chip out for a throw-in. This time Leeds take it short and try to engineer a crossing opportunity but go back to Trafford when they can’t find space.

Mbeumo’s on fire tonight as he has been all pre-season, causing Leeds problems whenever he runs at the defence. Now he storms down the centre-right and arcs a shot from 18 yards that beats Trafford’s leap and crashes into the underside of the crossbar. Bornauw hacks it away.

Amass tries to play a one-two with Zirkzee but the crucial middle pass of the three, from Zirkzee, goes astray.

Trafford dives to catch Dorgu’s cross. But he then boots his punt out for a throw-in and Tanaka is penalised for tussling with Dorgu who was thrown the ball and set off on a dribble down the inside-right.

Bikol heads Longstaff’s free-kick from the right over the bar after clever work from Bogle to earn the opportunity. .

Manchester United 1 Leeds United 1 (Aaronson) James robs Tyler Fletcher in the inside-left position and sprints towards the 18-yard line before slipping it inside to Aaronson. The once erratic finisher takes a touch to put Heaven on his heels then slots a right-foot shot crisply into the bottom left corner.

Leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6

Tanaka has two long throws in from the right. Dorgu heads the first one out for the second which is flicked on by Bornauw but Man Utd clear the second ball.

Tyler Fletcher takes a trick out of his old man’s book by grabbing James round the waist once the speed merchant had knocked the ball past him. Leeds go backwards from the free-kick as Man Utd’s press hounds them.

Trafford confidently catches the cross from the corner then bowls it out 40 yards to set Aaronson off on a counter. His solo raid down the right is stymied by Amass’s diligent defending.

Mbeumo drives down the gap between Muharemovic and Bijol, tries to find Doegu but Bornauw slides in to intercept but only succeeds in playing it back to Mbeumo who lashes a left-foot shot that Trafford tips round the right post at full stretch.

Top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA

There is certainly more urgency about Manchester United’s play. Leeds are living dangerously.

In the couple of minutes after the goal Manchester United almost punish Leeds’ high defensive line again but Muharemovic rides to the rescue. Bijol is a very good box defender but he lacks pace.

United’s start has been bright and confident and the system they playing is flipping between 4-4-2 and 4-2-3-1 and the first thought is always to go forward. The goal they have just scored is indicative of how they have started and it’s a positive for Joshua Zirkzee, who has spent much of his time at Old Trafford under a cloud, to have finished it with aplomb. Whether it will be enough to keep him at Old Trafford for the long run remains to be seen, particularly as interest from Italy persists, but what can’t be doubted is his attitude. He looks sharp.

Manchester United 1 Leeds United 0 (Zirkzee) Leeds, on the attack, lose possession down the middle and Dorgu works it out to Mbeumo who beats Bijol 20 yards inside the Man Utd half. Devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n

Manchester United build slowly down the right and then Dalot injects some urgency by whipping in a low cross. Zirkzee meets it not so much with a shot but with the timing of his arrival on the ball, deflecting it towards the right of goal powerfully, Trafford gets down well to save.

Leeds cross the free-kick into the box and James’ volley strikes a defender in the midriff and then hits the deck when going for the rebound, bundled over by Yoro. The ref waves play on and Manchester Unted counter with Amad Diallo dribbling down the right until tackled by Chadwick at the price of a corner.

Dorgu is penalised for a scissors-tackle on Bornauw. He did get the ball but only after he had caught he blond defender with his other leg. Carrick leaps up to protest, as does Farke but he is saying that Dorgu has twice slid in wildly.

Leeds defend the corner fairly solidly but Manchester United recover possession 30 yards out and set up Dalot to have a crack with a dipping, swerving effort that Trafford pats down in front of his face and catches after it bounces.

Amad Diallo finds Mbeumo down the right and he tries to head the ball across the box but Muharemovic is well-placed to head it back out but an attempt to nod the ball back to Trafford goes astray and the £45m man can’t stop it going out for a corner.

Leeds free-kick for either a foul by Amass on Aaronson or Dorgu on Bogle. Hard to tell, one was a split-second after the other.

Amass pulls back Bogle after being tackled by the Leeds wing-back and Leeds build up the right from the free-kick, earning themselves a throw-in parallel with the penalty spot. In Ampadu’s absence Tanaka is the trebuchet, hurling in the long throw that Bornauw nods on but Manchester united clear the second ball.

Leeds work the ball back to Taafford from the kick off and he chips it long up the right. Dorgu heads it out for a throw-in. Leeds go backwards again and pass the ball around confidently.

Jaka Bijol captains Leeds, Diogo Dalot leads out Manchester United.

They would be as well delaying the start of the game here the concourses outside this magnificent and historic stadium are packed with crowds taking in the solar eclipse. What a genuinely extraordinary moment! There will be plenty of time later this evening to talk about the football, for now attentions are firmly elsewhere!

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester United and Leeds United at a sold-out Croke Park in Dublin. Last year Leeds played Milan in the Irish capital and drew a crowd of 52,000 but at the GAA citadel, as I think I’m contractually obliged to call it, there will be 83,000 present, a testament to the Premier League’s reach and these two clubs’ popularity in Ireland founded on the exploits of Billy Whelan, Noel Cantwell, Johnny Giles, Roy Keane, Gary Kelly et al. It’s the first club match ever held at the stadium.

It’s a fixture that always stirs the blood and whenever it comes around you can guarantee that there will be reams of stuff about the War of the Roses, clash in styles, Busby and Revie, Bobby and Jack, large swathes of which this author has been guilty of producing. I’ll spare you all that today because while it’s relevant to fans of both clubs, they know it backwards. And it’s a match that has come around a wee bit too frequently in pre-season recently, first in Perth, Western Australia, in 2019 when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s side beat Marcelo Bielsa’s 4-0, then in 2023 in Oslo when Erik ten Haag’s second or third string defeated Daniel Farke’s threadbare, just relegated squad 2-0 and last year in Stockholm, which ended in a 0-0 draw between two scratch sides.

This one comes round later in the pre-season schedule than those three so we can expect to see stronger XIs, at least for part of the game. Leeds’ pre-season has gone well: after a 3-2 defeat by Wrexham in Tampa, they have beaten Sunderland in New Jersey, Liverpool in Chicago and RB Leipzig at Elland Road. Manchester United also lost to Wrexham (in Helsinki) then beat Rosenborg in Trondheim, Atlético in Stockholm and drew one apiece with the European champions, PSG, in Gothenburg last time out.

While Leeds will have new signing James Trafford available and Noah Okafor, who scored twice in Leeds’ first league victory at Old Trafford for 45 years last April, in the squad for the first time after the World Cup, Manchester United have Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford back in training since the start of the week but it seems too soon for them to start but Youri Tielemans is pushing to make his first start.

#1840. Sierra Leone vs Congo DR - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Ojele | 15 Nov 2026 23:31, Last updated: 15 Nov 2026 23:32

Sierra Leone and Congo DR return to action in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers when they square off in the second of their Group E double-header at the Stade El Abdi on Tuesday.

While the Leopards will look to maintain their 100% record in the qualifiers and move another step closer to securing their place in next year’s continental showpiece, Sierra Leone head into the game under considerable pressure for a result, having lost their three matches so far.

Tasked with guiding Sierra Leone to a first Africa Cup of Nations tournament since 2022, French head coach Didier Gomes Da Rosa has failed to make his mark in the qualifiers, with the Lone Stars rooted to the bottom of Group E after the first half of the campaign.

While they showed signs of promise, Sierra Leone blew a two-goal lead in the group opener on September 24, when they fell to a 3-2 loss against Zimbabwe in Morocco, four days before suffering a 1-0 loss at the hands of Equatorial Guinea at the Stade Omnisport Ahmadou Ahidjo.

Sierra Leone were left with a mountain to climb in the qualifiers on Thursday, when they were beaten 3-1 by DR Congo, with Yoane Wissa, Samuel Moutoussamy and Watford man Edo Kayembe hitting the back of the net to fire the Leopards to all three points.

Having missed out on the 2025 AFCON after an underwhelming qualifying campaign that saw them finish third in Group G with five points from six matches, Sierra Leone are one of just six sides yet to pick up any points in the qualifiers, leaving them with little margin for further errors and in need of significant improvement.

Meanwhile, Congo DR kicked off their AFCON qualifying journey on a high, claiming a 2-0 victory over Equatorial Guinea on September 24, four days before edging out Zimbabwe 2-1 at the National Sports Stadium thanks to strikes from Wissa and Moutoussamy.

However, a break from competitive action saw the Leopards fail to win their subsequent two outings, losing 2-0 against Uganda on October 2, three days before playing out a 1-1 stalemate with the Cranes in the second of their friendly double-header at the FNB Stadium.

Congo DR returned to action in the AFCON qualifiers with a comprehensive team display against Sierra Leone on Thursday to remain one of just four nations with a 100% record in the campaign and move one step closer to sealing a third appearance in the continental tournament since missing out in 2021.

Sebastien Desabre’s men, who are currently 40th in the latest FIFA World Rankings, sit top of the Group E standings with nine points from a possible nine, five points above Zimbabwe and Equatorial Guinea, who sit level on four points after the first three games.

Congo DR will be backing themselves to maintain their perfect record on Tuesday when they take on an opposing side who have lost each of their previous four meetings, conceding 11 goals and scoring just twice since September 2014.

Sierra Leone Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Congo DR Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Sierra Leone came out unscathed against DR Congo on Thursday, and we expect Da Rosa to name a similar XI at the Stade El Abdi, with Alie Conteh and Elfsborg striker Momoh Kamara spearheading the attack.

Amidst their struggles at the defensive end of the pitch, Da Rosa could opt for a change in the back four, with Alpha Turay, who made his debut in June 2023, coming into the mix to form the centre-back pairing with Kilmarnock man Michael John Kamara.

As for DR Congo, APS Atromitos Athinon midfielder Moutoussamy was forced off injured midway through Thursday’s clash, and the 30-year-old is a doubt for Tuesday’s matchup.

Should he fail to shake off the injury, Lorient man Noah Mbamba, who made his debut on Thursday, will push for his first start in the Leopards’ colours, teaming up with Edo Kayembe and Sunderland man Noah Sadiki at the centre of the park.

Up top, Wissa made it three goals in three AFCON qualifying games with his opener against Sierra Leone on Thursday, and the Newcastle United striker should lead the attack once again, forming the front three with Nathanael Mbuku and Almeria winger Brian Cipenga.

With three games played already, Tuesday’s result will prove decisive in determining Sierra Leone’s qualifying fate, and we expect the Lone Stars to go all out at the Stade El Abdi as they look to get their campaign back on track.

Congo DR, who have shown their class in Group E so far, boast the quality and experience across the pitch to get the result here, and we are backing them to continue from where they left off on Thursday, extending their hot streak against Sierra Leone.

#1839. Prediction: Athletic Bilbao vs Espanyol

Two camps who will make their respective returns from November’s international break on Friday night, Athletic Bilbao will welcome Espanyol to San Mames.

With the rest of Europe’s elite domestic leagues stealing centre stage this weekend, there are plenty of eye-catching betting promotions available.

Ahead of Friday’s La Liga showdown from the Basque Country, you can find all of the key Athletic Bilbao vs Espanyol H2H stats here.

Verdict: Athletic Bilbao win & Under 4.5 goals

Starting with the hosts, while Athletic Bilbao might still be searching for some recent stability, the Lions mark their return on Friday night at the heart of a European scrap. Suffering last-gasp heartbreak away at Osasuna prior to November’s international break as they eventually settled for a 1-1 stalemate in Navarre, Edin Terzic’s men will be seeking an immediate response at San Mames. Signing off October with a season-best performance as they stormed their way to an emphatic 4-0 victory against Getafe, the former Borussia Dortmund boss has seen his squad register seven points from their previous three La Liga appearances. Clinching local bragging rights against arch-rivals Real Sociedad earlier in the month as they opened November with a dramatic 2-1 victory, Bilbao know that three points on Friday night would temporarily skyrocket them into the European spots.

Both still recovering from respective knee injuries, Athletic Bilbao will once again be without the academy graduate duo of Unai Egiluz and Gorka Guruzeta. Watching their Copa del Rey adventure come to a remarkable end at the hands of fourth-tier outfit Sestao last month, Espanyol look set for what will be another stern examination when they travel to the Basque Country this weekend. In fact, their shock 1-0 win against Villarreal on October 30th is the only domestic victory that Sarabia’s side have mustered from their previous eight appearances across all competitions.

Yet to make a maiden appearance this season after undergoing hamstring surgery back in August, Espanyol will once again be without veteran marksman Kike Garcia here. However, serving a one-match La Liga suspension prior to November’s international break, 21-year-old Roger Hinojo will return to Sarabia’s travelling squad.

Completing a season-long loan switch from Burnley over the summer, Dutch defender Quilindschy Hartman will feature at the back. Notching six La Liga strikes so far this season, one-time Barcelona youngster Roberto Fernandez will lead Espanyol’s attack at San Mames.

Registering seven points in their final three La Liga appearances prior to November’s fortnight interval, Athletic Bilbao will now have their sights set on finding a route into the European spots. Gaining a reputation for their rugged success at San Mames and unbeaten in all of their previous five consecutive domestic battles in the Basque Country, Friday’s hosts should be smelling a potential opportunity here. It should also be highlighted, Bilbao have registered back-to-back wins in front of their own supporters for the first time this calendar year.

Verdict: Athletic Bilbao win & Under 4.5 goals

#1837. Five reasons England can win 2027 Nations League

England are one of the most likely teams to win the Nations League next summer, and after Sunday’s heroic 10-man win in Spain they will be speaking about their chances just as openly and brashly as that.

Having topped their group ahead of the world champions, they know they will face a group runner-up in March’s quarter-finals, and that could mean a tasty-looking two-legged tie against Belgium or Germany.

Their sights will be set further into the distance, though — June’s Nations League Finals, comprising of four teams, presenting a golden opportunity for England to win their first serious silverware since the 1966 World Cup. Here’s why they can do it…

This is something that has long been true of England and predates Thomas Tuchel’s time in charge. Of course, their tournament runs naturally tend to be brought to an end by top teams, but it so often against tougher opponents in previous knockout rounds or other competitions when England also produce their best football.

The Three Lions have often struggled to break down well-drilled teams who seek to defend deep against them — e.g. Ghana, Hungary or Slovenia — but teams that come out and take the game to them often bring out the best in England.

In 2026 alone, they have defeated Croatia three times out of three (13-3 on aggregate) as well as France, Erling Haaland’s Norway, and Mexico at the Estadio Azteca during the World Cup.

Then on Sunday came one of the finest victories in the national team’s 154-year history as they beat world champions Spain 3-2 in Madrid, the first time they had ever avoided defeat in a match against the team ranked No1 in the world.

Almost more so than the World Cup or European Championships, the Nations League guarantees regular meetings with the truly elite teams. England have proven they can unsettle and unpick the world’s very best.

Among reasons why England can win the Nations League in 2027, this one, more than any other, speaks for itself.

Discounting that barmy 6-4 third-place play-off win over France in which neither player started, England’s two best players scored 12 of the team’s World Cup 13 goals. And since returning for the new season, their levels have not dropped. According to the Gradient Sports’ model for overall performance, Bellingham has been the very best player across Europe’s top five leagues this term, with Kane not far behind in fifth.

Kane may now be 33 but is in the peak of his career and last month lifted the Ballon d’Or. And in Bellingham, England have a truly unique player, masterful at all aspects of the game and with a level of supreme self-belief that teases a similar self-assuredness out of those around him. England can win something while they have both in this imperious state.

For decades it has felt as though England’s midfield either did not possess enough genuine star quality, or did but was unable to function despite housing big names. Now, though, with Elliot Anderson, Declan Rice and Bellingham ahead of them, it seems England can at last dominate in the middle of the park and may no longer need to be solely reliant on counter-attacking when facing the world’s best sides.

London City player called up as Wiegman names latest England squad

Rediscover your adventurous side on an exotic getaway

When Rice missed the last international break, in came Alex Scott to partner Anderson and the balance produced helped to deliver a blistering 7-0 win in Rijeka, Croatia’s heaviest-ever defeat.

Back in came Rice this month and he and Anderson complemented each other superbly as all-action anchors in Madrid until Anderson’s sending off and England’s 10-man survival job. Up to the red card, England’s pass completion rate was better than Spain’s — almost unheard of.

England have embraced the Premier League and modern club football over the past eight years or so in order to become far more like a club team themselves, and the way Tuchel’s team is evolving just so happens to introduce a couple of club link-ups that are already improving on-field chemistry.

On the left, Lewis Hall of Newcastle United is making the left-back position his own. And further forward he can interchange with a player he knows very well indeed. Barcelona winger Anthony Gordon stepped up his game in an England shirt in 2026 and earned his move to Catalonia following three and a half years at Newcastle. It is clear they know each other’s games inside out.

The opposite flank has the potential to become all about Arsenal. Ben White scored England’s third against Spain and is well-placed to nail down the right-back position in 2027. Alongside him in England’s strongest XI would be the Three Lions’ best centre-back, Ezri Konsa, and in midfield, Rice. On the right wing, once back fit: Bukayo Saka. An Arsenal quartet playing with each other week in, week out would only help England’s coherence on the pitch.

Here is a factor not to be underestimated. Spain, Portugal and France will all join England among the eight quarter-finalists in March, but they have all won trophies in recent years.

England have been just about the most consistent team in international football not just in Europe but right across the world since Gareth Southgate’s team reached the 2018 World Cup semi-finals, and yet a succession of quite or very near misses has still left them without silverware. The years of hurt continue as winning the World Cup in 1966 becomes an ever-more distant memory.

It is the common view, though, that the greatest period in England’s men’s history is the one we are currently in, and a trophy of some sort at some point does feel an inevitability.

Bellingham, Kane and Tuchel all possess the self-confidence and courage England need to finally conquer that final mountain. Gordon and Rice share the same winning mentality. England are one of the very best teams in the world and have nothing to fear. And, crucially, they may want it just that little bit more.

#1836. Singapore vs Brazil - prediction, team news, lineups

By Freddie Cotton | 15 Nov 2026 23:35

Singapore welcome Brazil to the Singapore National Stadium on Tuesday morning for their final international fixture of the calendar year.

In their previous outing, the Lions fell to a damning defeat against Paraguay, while Selecao conceded in additional time to lose 3-2 to Japan.

After a disappointing ASEAN Championship campaign, bowing out to Thailand in the semi-finals to deny themselves of a first crown in seven tournament editions, Singapore have endured a tough run of results to close out the calendar year.

Having fallen to defeat against Indonesia in their opening ASEAN Cup fixture in September, the Lions did well to bounce back with a narrow victory over Bangladesh, but after suffering a thumping 6-0 loss to Malaysia in their final group match, Gavin Lee’s men failed to qualify for the knockout stages.

Singapore have so far been unsuccessful in their attempt to bounce back during the current international break too, having endured a resounding 4-1 defeat against Paraguay on home soil last week, making it just the two victories in their previous eight outings.

However, facing Brazil for the very first time, the Lions have the opportunity to forget about their recent woes on Tuesday morning by claiming a historic victory against Selecao, in what would be the highest-ranked FIFA opposition the hosts have ever overcome.

Following last year’s mediocre World Cup qualification campaign, in which they finished fifth out of 10 South American nations and squeezing through to the competition finals, Brazil will undoubtedly be underwhelmed with how they performed in the summer’s tournament.

Despite concluding the group stage at the summit of the Group C table, pipping Morocco to top spot on goal difference, and edging past Japan in their first knockout fixture, Selecao’s tournament came to a premature end at the quarterfinal stage as they suffered a convincing 2-0 defeat to Norway.

Much like their opposition, Carlo Ancelotti’s men have failed to fight back from their tournament woes in recent friendlies too as although they have won two of their previous four matches, Brazil have faced much weaker opposition and head into Tuesday’s clash off the back of a disappointing defeat to Japan at the weekend.

If Selecao are to respond quickly, one of their biggest avenues for improvement is their defensive solidity, with Ancelotti’s side keeping just three clean sheets in their previous 14 games and conceding five goals over their latest three matches.

Having picked up no fresh injury concerns against Paraguay, Singapore head into Tuesday’s match with a predominantly fit squad, though the hosts are still without defender Nur Abdullah as the 25-year-old continues his recovery from an ACL injury.

After netting the equaliser on Friday, Ui-Young Song is almost certain to start in the Lions’ attack once again against Brazil, likely alongside fellow Lion City Sailors club teammates Farhan Zulkifli and Ilhan Fandi.

Following his red card in the dying stages of Saturday’s clash with Japan, 29-year-old forward Raphinha will be unavailable this week for Brazil, alongside Ancelotti, who will be absent from the sidelines having been sent off just moments later.

In the Barcelona winger’s absence, Ancelotti will be hoping that Vinicius Junior can continue his hot streak for Selecao, having netted both goals in the defeat to the Samurai Blue after a rocky patch to start the season for Real Madrid.

However, the visitors are missing multiple of their big hitters, with Gabriel Martinelli, Joao Pedro and Lucas Paqueta among those to be sidelined and unavailable for Brazil this week.

Mahbud; R.Stewart, Harun, Mahler, Baharudin; Nakamura, Shahiran; Zulkifli, H.Stewart, Song; Fandi

Bento; Wesley Franca, Cunha, Gabriel, Carlos Augusto; Guimaraes, Santos, Gomes; Estevao, Endrick, Vinicius Junior

With Selecao struggling to string a run of form together, Singapore can certainly be forgiven for having aspirations of a giant killing this week, especially on home soil.

However, despite their difficulties, we think Brazil will bounce straight back on Tuesday morning with a convincing victory at the Singapore National Stadium.

#1834. Kenya vs South Africa - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 15 Nov 2026 23:55

Kenya host South Africa in a 2027 Africa Cup of Nations Group D qualifier at Nyayo National Stadium in Nairobi on Tuesday.

The return leg arrives four days after substitute Ryan Ogam’s 90th-minute strike earned Harambee Stars a 2-2 draw in Soweto, a result that cut Pitso Mosimane’s lead at the top of the group to a single point over Guinea.

Kenya have taken two points from three Group D games, drawing 1-1 with Eritrea at Nyayo National Stadium, losing 1-0 away to Guinea and then drawing 2-2 in Soweto.

Qualification for the finals is already secured because Kenya co-host the tournament with Uganda and Tanzania, so only one non-host team from the group will advance and Benni McCarthy’s side are chasing a first win of the campaign rather than a place.

Kenya conceded in all three qualifiers, and the first leg followed the pattern: Amos Wanjala, who started in defensive midfield, sent a heavy backpass into his own net in the ninth minute, Michael Olunga levelled from the penalty spot in the 44th minute after Thabang Matuludi handled, and Ogam struck after Olwethu Makhanya was dispossessed.

McCarthy said his side struggled with South Africa’s full-backs until he moved to a back three early in the second half, with the wing-backs tasked with occupying them.

He has promised a more aggressive approach at home and pointed to Nairobi’s altitude and climate as conditions his players know and the visitors may not.

Olunga’s penalty was his 35th goal for Kenya, level with William Ouma as the national record scorer, and one more would make him the outright leader less than a week after returning from roughly five months out with a pelvic injury that required surgery in Paris.

Ogam, who plays for RFC Liege, has scored two of Kenya’s three group goals, an 87th-minute equaliser against Eritrea and the late leveller in Soweto, the first open-play goal Kenya have scored against South Africa.

McCarthy, born in Cape Town and South Africa’s record international scorer with 31 goals, was facing his native country as a head coach in a competitive match for the first time, and President William Ruto has urged supporters to fill Nyayo National Stadium for the return.

South Africa arrive in Nairobi with seven points from three games, one ahead of Guinea, after beating Guinea 2-1 and Eritrea 5-0 before the draw in Soweto.

The 2-2 result was the first time Bafana Bafana dropped points since Mosimane returned as head coach, and they led twice without being able to hold on.

Relebohile Mofokeng of Union Saint-Gilloise now has three qualifying goals, two in the 5-0 win over Eritrea and the 77th-minute finish in Soweto that followed a pass from substitute Lyle Foster.

Mosimane’s side have scored nine and conceded three in three games, and both Kenya goals in Soweto came from defensive lapses, with Matuludi’s handball giving away the penalty and Makhanya failing to clear before Ogam won the ball.

Mbekezeli Mbokazi, who missed the wins over Guinea and Eritrea with a thigh injury, is available again after being left out of the first-leg XI, and Makhanya is the obvious player to make way.

South Africa have never lost to Kenya in normal time, with three wins and a 1-1 draw in four previous friendlies, although Kenya won the 2002 penalty shootout that followed that draw.

Mosimane said the squad took the first available flight to Nairobi, leaving at 01:00 on Saturday and landing at around 06:00, and that no player reported fatigue when the group trained on Sunday.

Kenya Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

South Africa Africa Cup of Nations Qualifying form:

Kenya have no suspensions reported, and Olunga and defender Eric Ouma are back after long injury layoffs, with Ouma used as a substitute in Soweto.

Wrexham defender Zak Vyner was left out of the first leg because of a paperwork problem, and McCarthy said he was hopeful that it would be resolved in time for Tuesday, which would allow the uncapped 29-year-old to make his debut.

Olunga was replaced by Micah Obiero in the second half in Soweto, so the captain’s match fitness is the main selection question, while Ogam is pushing for a start after coming off the bench to score.

Byrne Odhiambo, Frank Odhiambo, Sylvester Owino, Abud Omar and Rooney Onyango all started in the first leg, and McCarthy used Wanjala in midfield before moving him into a back three.

For South Africa, Mosimane has the full squad available, with no suspensions, although centre-backs Ime Okon and Makhanya each carry one yellow card and a second caution would rule them out of their next qualifier.

Goalkeeper Ronwen Williams and midfielder Teboho Mokoena were fitness doubts after missing Mamelodi Sundowns matches, yet both started in Soweto, while Thapelo Maseko missed the squad through injury and Themba Zwane and Nkosinathi Sibisi were left out.

Williams will want to bounce back after Olunga sent him the wrong way from the spot, a penalty McCarthy highlighted because the goalkeeper is regarded as one of the best penalty stoppers in Africa.

Up front, Oswin Appollis, Tshepang Moremi and Iqraam Rayners started in Soweto, with Foster and Puso Dithejane replacing Moremi and Rayners in the second half and lifting the side.

B. Odhiambo; Wanjala, F. Odhiambo, Owino; Omar, Tera, J. Ochieng, R. Onyango; Wilson, Olunga, Ogam

Williams; Matuludi, Mbokazi, Okon, Modiba; Sithole, Mokoena; Appollis, Mofokeng, Moremi; Foster

South Africa have the sharper attack, with nine goals in three games against Kenya’s three, and Mofokeng, Appollis and Moremi should find space on the flanks if McCarthy follows through on his promise to push higher up the pitch.

Kenya’s counter-argument is strong, because the back-three adjustment worked in Soweto, Nairobi’s altitude is a real factor, and Olunga needs one goal to hold the national scoring record outright.

Even so, Kenya have conceded in all three qualifiers and have not kept a clean sheet, while Mosimane can restore Mbokazi to fix the problem that cost his side two points.

A team that has twice squandered a lead should respond with more control, and South Africa’s depth up front should be enough to take a narrow win, with Olunga or Ogam likely to give Kenya a consolation.

Manchester United are set to make history with the appointment of Silvia Tuya as part of Mauricio Pochettino’s backroom staff.

But Pochettino will also bring newer additions to his coaching team, including strength and conditioning coach Tuya in what will be a first for Man United.

The strength and conditioning coach will be familiar with creating such history, having previously become the first female coach in the history of the USMNT’s senior squad when she joined the backroom staff in October 2024.

Tuya holds a doctorate of science in high performance and is fluent in English, Spanish, and Catalan.

She has previously lectured at the University of Barcelona and National Institute of Physical Education of Catalonia, before joining Pochettino’s USA set up in October 2024.

Prior to the move to the States, the Spaniard briefly worked with FC Badalona in her native Catalonia, the team competing in Liga F - the top-flight of the women’s game in Spain.

Tuya also worked with Levante’s women's team, and has experience in strength and conditioning athletes from other disciplines, such as tennis, rugby, basketball, and ironman competitors.

The specialist in strength and conditioning was in charge of physical preparation at Levante, and will likely work closely with fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino - son of Mauricio - at Man United.

A PhD fellow, Tuya has contributed to different scientific papers, including research into reactions in football.

While certain members of Pochettino’s backroom staff have already travelled to England, the Guardian claim Tuya, analyst Alec Scott and Miguel D’Agostino have remained with the USA camp ahead of the CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final second leg with Haiti.

As such, Tuya will be expected to start work at Carrington from November 18 - the same day as Pochettino.

Man United agreed that Pochettino could take charge of the USA’s games against Haiti before starting work at Carrington and Old Trafford.

#1832. Goodwin and Cox earn first England call-ups for World Cup play-off

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Isobel Goodwin and Katie Cox have received their first England call-ups for the World Cup play-off against Ukraine, while Ella Toone returns.

Goodwin scored her third Women's Super League goal of the season in a 1-1 draw against Arsenal at Emirates Stadium on Sunday, when Lionesses boss Sarina Wiegman was in the stands.

Cox, 20, is on loan at WSL 2 side Nottingham Forest from Chelsea and has kept one clean sheet in four appearances this term.

After initially being dropped from the side in October, Toone replaced the injured Lucy Bronze and has done enough to convince Wiegman she warrants a place against Ukraine.

There is also a spot for Aggie Beever-Jones due to Chelsea team-mate Lauren James' injury, while Grace Clinton and Poppy Pattinson return to the fold too.

Grace Frisk, Frey Godfrey, Erica Meg Parkinson and Lexi Potter all hold onto their places after debuting in the 8-1 aggregate victory over Greece in the first round of the play-offs.

The first leg against Ukraine will take place in Murcia on December 1 before the return leg at Wembley on December 5.

Wiegman said: "We know what’s at stake in these games and our focus is on producing two strong performances to secure our place at the World Cup.

"We have worked hard to put ourselves in this position and now we have to finish the job. Ukraine will provide a challenge and we will prepare with the same focus and determination that we always do.

#1830. Tottenham starting to carve out new identity under Roberto De Zerbi as rest of season predicted

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau

After a tricky start to the season, Tottenham have begun to find their feet under Roberto De Zerbi.

Despite spending more than £300million on new players over the summer, Spurs were bottom of the Premier League table before the September international break.

They have since found form, though, losing just one of their next five games and, after an unbeaten October, De Zerbi was crowned Premier League Manager of the Month last week.

Spurs endured a nightmare opening weekend as their expensively assembled squad was dismantled 3-0 by Brentford at the Gtech Community Stadium.

Performances have since improved, though, and Spurs produced a result for the ages when they beat Chelsea 2-0 at Stamford Bridge to secure just their second win in 42 attempts at the Blues’ home ground.

Defeat to Leeds in their last game was a setback, but overall performances have steadily evolved, and Spurs are starting to carve out an identity under De Zerbi.

Spurs embarked on a comprehensive squad overhaul during the summer as they parted ways with a number of senior players while also looking to build a team in De Zerbi’s image.

The addition of centre-back Jan Paul van Hecke, who worked under De Zerbi at Brighton, has proven an astute piece of business, and he has begun to develop a solid partnership with fellow Dutch international Micky van de Ven.

In midfield, Spurs went big, splashing £185m on Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali. The pair have taken a bit of time to acclimatise, but recently they have begun to develop an understanding with each other.

There is still a lot more to come, though, from Spurs’ attacking signings, with Savio and Mykhailo Mudryk struggling for fitness while striker Omar Marmoush has flattered to deceive since arriving from Manchester City.

Having guided Spurs to Premier League survival last season, De Zerbi has plenty of goodwill in the bank, and it is why his job didn’t come under serious scrutiny when Spurs failed to win any of their first five league games.

The Italian’s substitutions have drawn criticism, and Spurs still struggle to react to going behind, but overall De Zerbi has his team playing with intensity and personality.

Issues still persist in attack, but that is as much down to personnel as it is De Zerbi’s tactics. Either way, though, he will have to find a way to make Spurs more efficient in the final third.

The midfielder began talks with the club over improved terms earlier in the year and those have accelerated in recent weeks.

It is understood that a verbal agreement has now been reached and Rice will soon put pen to paper on the deal.

Newcastle have no intention of selling Lewis Hall in January despite growing interest in the England international.

The 22-year-old has established himself as Thomas Tuchel’s first-choice left-back following impressive performances against Croatia and Spain, attracting attention from clubs across Europe.

Manchester United made an approach for Hall last summer but were told he was not for sale, before the defender signed a new long-term contract in September.

According to The Telegraph, Newcastle are likely to demand well over £80m for a defender contracted until 2031.

Barcelona, Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain could also emerge as potential suitors.

According to FootballTransfers, the Gunners still view the 26-year-old as their leading target to strengthen the left wing, with senior figures believing a deal could be possible as early as next summer.

Vinicius has struggled for consistency this season and faces competition from new signing Yan Diomande for a starting place.

Manchester United’s alternative targets to Mauricio Pochettino have been revealed.

It left the Premier League side mired in the top-flight relegation zone, and searching for their eighth permanent head coach since Sir Alex Ferguson’s retirement in 2013.

Vinicius Junior has admitted that Arsenal’s push to sign him in the summer has impacted his form this season.

The Gunners held strong interest in him as they looked to kick on from their Premier League title win and make a marquee signing in attack.

Vinicius had entered the final 12 months of his contract at Real Madrid in the summer and there was strong speculation that he could leave the club.

With Real and Vinicius at a contract impasse and little progress made in negotiations, Arsenal made it clear they would meet the winger’s financial demands.

Mikel Arteta was desperate to sign the 26-year-old but the Brazilian ultimately ended up signing a new six-contract at the Santiago Bernabeu.

However, Vinicius has had an unhappy time at Real this season. In 12 appearances under Jose Mourinho, he has registered just one goal and three assists.

#1828. Monday's Nations League predictions including Germany vs Netherlands, Greece vs Serbia

By Ellis Stevens | 16 Nov 2026 00:00

Today's UEFA Nations League predictions include a battle for top spot in League A Group 2, with Germany taking on Netherlands, while Greece are looking to take three points against Serbia to keep their hopes of finishing in the top two alive.

Faroe Islands play host to Moldova on Monday night looking for the win that would see them finish in second place in Group C3 of the UEFA Nations League.

However, the visitors only require a draw to ensure that they qualify for the promotion playoffs.

After their surprise draw in Slovakia, Faroe Islands will be full of confidence for this contest. However, Moldova are on their own high, and we feel that the visitors to Torshavn will do enough to earn the share of the spoils that they require for second place.

Slovakia square off against Kazakhstan on Monday having already secured top spot in Group C3 of the UEFA Nations League.

In sharp contrast to the visitors earning promotion with a game to spare, Kazakhstan must win this fixture to have any chance of avoiding finishing bottom of the group.

Slovakia will be motivated to retain their unbeaten record in the group, leading us to back the visitors to avoid defeat. Nevertheless, Kazakhstan perform better on familiar territory than on their travels, so a low-scoring draw could play out.

Lithuania welcome Liechtenstein to the Darius and Girenas Stadium on Monday evening for the final round of League D fixtures in the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League campaign.

In their previous competition outing, Trispalves fell to a narrow 1-0 defeat against Azerbaijan, while Blau-Rot lost to Milli Komanda by the same scoreline on Friday evening.

With nothing to lose, Liechtenstein will be gunning to end their Nations League campaign on a high and claim their first victory over Lithuania in 15 years.

However, facing a Trispalves side who have lost just one of their previous five matches and took all three points when the nations met in September, it is difficult to see that happening and we predict the hosts to confirm a second-placed finish by winning on Monday evening.

Estonia will welcome Bulgaria to the Lillekula Stadium in Tallinn for Monday's UEFA Nations League encounter.

The hosts, who have secured a top-two finish, could still achieve automatic promotion, while the visitors only have pride to play for on the final matchday of the league phase.

Estonia have proven to be a tough team to break down in Group C4, and considering Bulgaria have failed to score in three of their last four games, we think the hosts could edge a cagey contest on Monday.

Iceland will look to wrap up automatic promotion when they welcome Luxembourg to Reykjavik for Monday's Nations League encounter.

The hosts are sitting two points at the top of Group C4, while the visitors are languishing at the bottom of the standings ahead of the final matchday of the league phase.

Iceland will be full of confidence after thrashing Bulgaria 5-0 last time out, and we think they will produce another free-scoring display against a Luxembourg side that are low on confidence after four consecutive defeats.

Gibraltar will be looking to finish their UEFA Nations League campaign on a positive note when they welcome Malta to Europa Point Stadium on Monday evening.

The visitors have already secured top spot in their League D group, while the hosts will be keen to pick up their first win.

Gibraltar should provide a tough test for Malta, but the visitors are unbeaten in the Nations League for a reason and should have enough quality to pick up the win.

Switzerland welcome Scotland to Berit Sitterstadion on Monday night for a matchday six clash in UEFA Nations League League B Group 1.

The hosts have already secured top spot heading into the final game, while the visitors are still battling to finish second and in the promotion playoff place.

Scotland may have more at stake but Switzerland have been the dominant force in League B Group 1, and we expect their unbeaten run to continue with another win here.

North Macedonia will welcome Slovenia to Tose Proeski Arena on Monday night for a matchday six clash in UEFA Nations League B Group 1.

The hosts' relegation to League C has already been confirmed, while the visitors are fighting to secure second place and a chance at promotion to League A.

Slovenia are undoubtedly the favourites to win this match, as demonstrated in their comfortable victory in the reverse fixture, and the visitors should secure all three points.

Fighting for a place in the UEFA Nations League quarter-finals, Germany are set to host League A's Group A2 leaders, the Netherlands, at Olympiastadion Berlin on Monday.

Die Mannschaft know that they likely need to win to progress, while Oranje are through barring an unprecedented swing in goal-difference.

The maths of the table may be complex, but Germany know that a simple victory will see them through to the quarter-finals.

Oranje have yet to lose in the Nations League this season, though with the stakes lowered, they could be caught off guard.

Under pressure in League A of the UEFA Nations League, Greece will welcome Serbia to Panthessaliko Stadium for their final Group A2 showdown on Monday.

The Azure and White are battling for a place in the quarter-finals, while the Eagles are competing to earn a place in the League A/B playoffs.

Greece may have been hammered 7-0 by the Netherlands last time out, but that defeat came as a shock, and with a place in the quarter-finals at stake, the hosts will be motivated to bounce back.

Serbia have struggled throughout this term's Nations League, and it would be surprising to see them avoid a sixth consecutive defeat on Monday.

#1827. ‘I wanted to score more!’ – Vinicius explains Brazil sub frustration

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Vinicius Junior's frustration at being substituted in Brazil's 7-0 demolition of Singapore was simply because he wanted to add to his hat-trick.

With three goals in the opening 21 minutes in the friendly at Singapore National Stadium, Vinicius scored his first senior international hat-trick in his 59th cap.

The Real Madrid winger fired home from an excellent Bruno Guimaraes pass in the ninth minute before Endrick and Estevao granted him simple finishes to put Brazil in control.

Vinicius had a goal ruled out before being replaced by Allan on the hour mark, and he was visibly irritated by the decision.

"It was agreed that I would play 15 or 20 minutes more. I always want to score more goals," said Vinicius.

"I understand that more people needed to play, like Allan. I could have scored more, but I'm happy for the victory."

Vinicius made his Brazil debut in 2019 and had previously bagged three braces for the Selecao, the latest of which came during Saturday's 3-2 loss to Japan.

#1824. Man United transfer news: Mauricio Pochettino faces battle for 'impressive' £21m centre-back from Liverpool and Chelsea

By Lewis Nolan | 16 Nov 2026 00:21

Manchester United share interest in AC Milan defender Koni De Winter with Liverpool and Chelsea, the newest report has claimed.

The Red Devils are preparing for the return of Premier League football, with Mauricio Pochettino set to take charge of his first game on November 22 against Liverpool.

There are concerns that his weak defence could cost the new head coach at Anfield, with the likes of Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez having struggled this season.

Recruiting new defenders should be seen as a priority, and it should come as no surprise to see the club linked with a host of talented stars.

Tuttomercatoweb report that United hold serious interest in AC Milan centre-back De Winter, who is valued by Transfermarkt at just under £21m, though they may face competition from the likes of Liverpool and Chelsea.

Pochettino is known to use an aggressive system, with the 54-year-old often asking defenders to step forward and press from the halfway line.

De Winter possesses immense speed, and the 24-year-old is far more mobile then any of United's current options at the back.

The Belgian has been trusted on the ball by Milan, with the centre-back so far averaging 61.1 successful passes per game in Serie A.

De Winter also wins most of his battles in the air, and he could be a sensible addition in either January or the summer.

Both Liverpool and Chelsea will almost certainly qualify for European competitions this season, whereas United are fighting a relegation battle.

However, the Reds may not need to sign a centre-back if Virgil van Dijk extends his stay beyond this summer, though the Blues are always active in the market.

Pochettino may find it hard to convince De Winter to join, especially if Chelsea secure either Champions League or Europa League football, and it remains to be seen if Old Trafford will still be the attraction it once was for transfer targets.

#1823. Raul Jimenez’s late penalty seals share of spoils for Wolves against Blackburn

An injury-time penalty from returning hero Raul Jimenez ensured Wolves came away with a point in their Championship opener after Blackburn had produced a comeback.

Wolves led through Marshall Munetsi’s cool finish on 18 minutes only for Sean McLoughlin’s first Blackburn goal to draw the visitors level on 27 minutes with a well-timed run and header.

The visitors turned the game around on 48 minutes through Andri Gudjohnsen’s close-range strike only for substitute Jimenez to level the game three minutes into injury time from the spot after Ryan Alebiosu handled the ball in the box. Jimenez and his wife marked his return to Molineux by giving 5,000 fans black scarves emblazoned with the words ‘Si Senor’ - a nod to his song - and Jimenez did not disappoint as he rifled in his penalty.

LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU

Cesar Peixoto wants Wolves to play with their heads rather than their hearts after the home side rescued a late point in the first game of the Championship season following relegation. Wolves replaced Rob Edwards with Portuguese coach Peixoto during the summer and he felt his side’s loss of organisation allowed Blackburn to take control of the game.

Peixoto said: “One point is not what we want, we want three points. We lost some organisation in the second half and played more with our hearts and not our heads and brains.

“We have to keep our mental stability during the 90 minutes because we’re better when we’re organised. We need to play our way with our identity. It’s a lesson for us to understand when we lose organisation it’s more difficult for us and more easy for the opposition.

“We’re working hard to bring more solutions [into the club] but we need to work hard with the players we have. It’s the first game, there’s a lot to work on and a lot to improve.”

Tony Mowbray took charge of Blackburn in the league for the first time since returning to the club for a second stint in the dugout. Rovers recorded their lowest league finish since Mowbray’s first stint in charge of the club last term but the Blackburn boss is confident his side have enough to beat the drop and climb up the table this campaign.

Mowbray said: “Ultimately, it feels like a defeat, it’s a bit disappointing and a bit frustrating. I just felt a lot of decisions were starting to swing their way. It’s harsh to take, I don’t think they deserved a second goal. We asked the players to be brave and we were collectively very strong.

“Everybody has us relegated, probably on the back of finishing 20th last season and losing a couple of our better players and not spending much money, which is a good motivation for the team. We deserved to win the game, we showed there’s enough quality to give teams problems and I hope there’s help on the way [in the transfer window].”

The first chance of the season came the way of Blackburn as a cross-field pass found Alebiosu down the right, who floated a ball into the box only for an unmarked Oladipo Afolayan to head wide from eight-yards out.

However, Wolves scored the first goal of the new campaign when Fer Lopez played a defence-splitting through ball into the path of Munetsi, who coolly found the net with a first time effort from the edge of the penalty area.

"A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq

Blackburn drew level through an unlikely source just nine minutes later as McLoughlin headed in his first-ever goal in English football in more than 150 games when he met Ryoya Morishita’s cross from the right at the near post.

The home side had chances to retake the lead before the break as Lopez curled a shot narrowly over the top from 20-yards while Kieran Trippier teed up Mateus Mane for a chance as the teenager found the top of the net from distance.

Blackburn turned the game on its head minutes after the break as Gudjohnsen turned home Afolayan’s deflected ball in from the right from close range to stun Molineux into silence.

"It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK

Peixoto introduced Jimenez from the bench on the hour mark but even the Mexican could not lift Wolves with Blackburn comfortable for long periods as frustration grew in the stands.

However, Alebiosu handled Jackson Tchatchoua’s cross from the left in injury time and the referee awarded a spot kick which allowed Jimenez to mark his Wolves return with an equaliser from 12-yards as he sent Balazs Toth the wrong way.

“I think it is a really harsh one. He [the referee] has to be sure at such a critical time of the game. And I do not think he can be sure. I think he has almost had a guess that he is in the box. It is such a big call.”

“We see the ref’s position. The fact the ref makes the decision to give the penalty in my opinion, it is a bigger decision to give it then to not. We have got the luxury of the replays and we are still not sure. His whole body is outside the box.”

“It looks outside the box to me [the penalty incident]. The still picture suggests to me it was outside the box. We can get better and we will have to. We have to be more dominant with the ball at times and be better in attack. We have done a lot of work on that in pre-season. Having been in this league a long time, the power of the dressing room is crucial and any motivation tool you can you use is important. I think we will be fine. You have to enjoy football and love it. I think the boys enjoyed it tonight.”

“Obviously frustrated. The boys did everything to get the three points but it is gutting in the end. I thought I was outside the box when the ball came in and the decision went against us. They are saying it is in the box and it is frustrating. We dug deep and thought we had it. I cannot fault everyone as we all put in a shift, it was just the final details with the penalty decision. We deserved the three points. If we play like that every week, we will go far in the table.”

Raul Jimenez reacts after his late penalty saved a point for Wolves against Blackburn 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/aXvVeWw6fc

“Before the game we were predicting Wolves would be right up there [this season] and we thought it would be a comfortable win. But that was not the case.  Blackburn gave a really good account of themselves and had lots of openings. [Cesar] Peixoto will be breathing a massive sigh of relief with that handball.”

“Wolves got away with one if I am being really honest. In terms of their second-half performance, they did not do anywhere near enough. I thought Blackburn were excellent throughout and deservedly took the lead. It is a huge decision [to give the penalty], but in the end Raul Jimenez steps up to get his side the point. [Cesar Peixoto] will be delighted to get something in the end.”

Bentley spills the corner but gets a free-kick. Moments later, the referee blows his whistle for the final time and the game ends level at 2-2. A dramatic opening night of the new Championship season at Molineux. If the Championship continues in this vein all season, it will be one hell of a year.

Blackburn nearly score a late winner as Garrett’s shot is tipped over the bar by Bentley for a later Blackburn corner.

He sends Toth the wrong way and calmly slots home to bring Wolves level in added time. That penalty decision will certainly create some debate. The Championship is always full of drama and we get some on opening night.

LATE DRAMA! 😱Raul Jimenez cooly converts from the penalty spot, deep into added time to save a point for Wolves 🔥 pic.twitter.com/5h2lMxcHNU

It just had to be. Jimenez rescues Wolves from the penalty spot.

Drama on the opening night of the campaign.

Relief for Wolves, heartbreak for Blackburn.

Late drama at Molineux! The cross is sent in from the left and the ball strikes the arm Alebiosu on the edge of the box. Was it inside or outside the penalty area? It is definitely handball but was it outside the box? It was very, very close but there is no VAR in the Championship so the penalty will stand.

Four added minutes. Are we on the verge of seeing the first shock of the new Championship season on opening night?

Four minutes added. Not even a reaction from the home crowd.

Wolves are desperately running out of time and Blackburn still look comfortable.

Home fans are beginning to filter out slowly.

Mosquera is still struggling but he has come back on whilst limping around. I cannot imagine there will be too much in terms of added time, either three or four minutes would be my guess, no more.

Ohashi is played in behind and goes down under a challenge from Toti on the edge of the Wolves box but those appeals are waved away.

Mosquera has gone down again and he may not be able to continue as he receives treatment on the sidelines. Wolves may be ending this game down to 10 men.

Fevrier’s shot from outside the Wolves penalty area is blocked and spins behind for a corner in front of the travelling Blackburn fans. The corner comes to nothing.

Wolves struggling to create anything of note even with Jimenez’s introduction.

Centre-back Mosquera has gone up front but appears to be struggling with an injury. He’s jogged back to his natural position now.

Desperate long balls being sent forward but Blackburn look comfortable for now. The home fans are quite audibly unhappy with this second-half showing.

Wolves do not currently look like scoring an equaliser.

Mosquera is struggling with a knock but Wolves made all five changes. If he is unable to continue, Wolves will have to finish off with ten men.

The frustration inside Molineux is growing and the home fans want to see some more urgency from their side as they trail with under 10 minutes left.

Blackburn are now going to make their final two alterations of the night as Ribeiro and Garrett come on.

Wolves are going to make their final two substitutions as Lima and Chirewa replace Moller Wolfe and Andre.

Blackburn are looking pretty comfortable right now defending their lead and counter-attacking effectively.

Wolves want a penalty as Armstrong goes down inside the box after making a run in behind but the appeals are waved away. Rightly so as Armstrong was not fouled.

Wolves are pushing to find an equaliser but are struggling to carve out many genuine opportunities.

Ohashi is penalised for a foul on F Lopez not far outside the Blackburn penalty area and that was pretty harsh on Ohashi. Jimenez is lining this one up as is F Lopez.

The former takes but his effort hits the wall.

Wolves’ frustration right now is summed up by a dreadful cross from F Lopez from the right side of the box that goes behind for a goal kick. The TV cameras then turn to some of the Wolves fans, who look rather forlorn in the stands.

Double changes for both sides. For Wolves, Doyle and Tchatchoua come on. For Blackburn, Fevrier and Ohasi enter the fray.

You’d have thought a goal had gone in such is the reaction from the home crowd to Jimenez’s introduction. I have to say, I’m surprised Mane has made way but Jimenez will play through the middle with Armstrong moved out to the left.

Blackburn made a change earlier in the half with Wolverhampton-born Sam Morsy on for his Rovers debut. One manager going for it as the other attempts to shore things up.

Wolves’ last shot on target was all the way back in the 18th minute, when Munetsi put them in front. That is in fact their only shot on target tonight, compared to Blackburn’s four.

Should Wolves have been given a penalty? Jimenez goes down after Atcheson did stick out his leg but was there enough in it to give a penalty?

Jimenez is indeed now going to come on and Molineux rises to welcome him onto the pitch. The Jimenez scarfs go up around the ground and his song is sung. Mane goes off.

Raúl Jiménez receives an incredible reception from the Wolves fans as he makes his league return for the club 👏🇲🇽 pic.twitter.com/mPE7pvTJZt

No messing about from new Wolves boss Cesar Peixoto with his side behind and discontent brewing in the stands, Raul Jimenez is going to be introduced. His name has been sung throughout the game with a hero’s welcome imminent.

Can he inspire a comeback? Wolves and Peixoto will certainly hope so.

Munetsi, the scorer of Wolves’ goal, has a shot deflected from the edge of the box and it goes behind for a corner. Gudjohnsen, the scorer of Blackburn’s second, heads away at the front post.

You can sense the frustration growing from the home fans inside Molineux, with a few groans creeping in.

Blackburn are the first to turn to their bench as one experienced midfielder replaces another with Morsy coming on for Forshaw.

Wow! What a start to the second half. Blackburn have turned it around, Tony Mowbray clearly inspired his troops at half time.

Molineux is silenced now with Blackburn fans making all the noise. Some home supporters were still taking their seats as Gudjohnsen turned the ball home.

Can Wolves turn the game back in their favour? It’s all a bit slow now from the hosts followed by the first signs of disgruntlement from the home supporters.

And to top it off, Mane is booked for simulation.

The first Wolves player into the book tonight is Mane and it is for simulation. Watching the replays, that feels like a fair call as Mane threw himself to the ground and it probably was a dive.

Molineux is stunned as the underdogs take the lead inside the opening five minutes of the second half. Tony Mowbray’s side have started well since the break and are rewarded. Afolayan is found making a run into the penalty area on the right side of the box and his cross is slotted home by Gudjohnsen. His father Eidur would have been happy with a striker’s finish like that.

"It's brilliantly worked by Blackburn Rovers!" 💥Andri Guðjohnsen finishes from close range to turn the game around and the visitors the lead 👏 pic.twitter.com/vkKQQezicK

Morishita drives forward through the Wolves half and towards the penalty area. He lays it off to Afolayan, whose effort is tipped over the bar by Bentley for a Blackburn corner, which is headed and then cleared away by Wolves.

We are back under way at Molineux. No changes for either side at the break.

An intriguing first half as the whistle sounds and both teams head down the tunnel.

Plenty to think about for the two managers.

The first half is brought to a close at Molineux and an engaging opening 45 minutes of the new Championship season results in this game being level at 1-1 at the break. Munetsi put Wolves in front before McLoughlin equalised for Blackburn.

Forshaw is the third Blackburn player into the book tonight as the referee goes back to penalise the midfielder for an earlier foul on Andre. That was not Forshaw’s first foul either.

With no VAR or hydration breaks, there will be just one added minute at the end of this first half.

Mane wins it back for his side on the edge of his own penalty area and drives forward. He takes it across the halfway line before feeding a lovely pass to his right to find Armstrong, whose shot is blocked.

Mane comes close to a stunner. Trippier rolls the ball across the face of the penalty area to 18-year-old Mane, who takes on the shot first time but his effort goes just over the bar.

Wolves come close to restoring their lead. Mane drives inside from the left and plays the ball forward to F Lopez, who takes one touch before getting his shot away from just outside the box. He tries to pick out the top corner but it just misses the target.

Like London buses, two yellow cards come at once and another Blackburn player is into the book. It is their captain Cantwell who receives a yellow card for delaying the restart. Cantwell was not too impressed with that decision.

Both teams off the mark for the season now, a brilliant near-post run and header from McLoughlin who scores his first-ever goal in English football to level the game up.

Molineux briefly stunned into silence. A slight delay from the fans celebrating the header as well.

The first booking of the Championship season goes the way of Blackburn left-back Pickering. It is a pretty simple decision for the referee as Pickering cynically pulls back R Gomes, who had spun him, and rightly receives a yellow card.

R Gomes delivers a cross from the right side of the Blackburn box across the penalty area but Armstrong does not pre-empt that and is not on hand to meet it. Morishita clips in the cross from the right to the near post, where McLoughlin meets it first and guides a powerful header into the far corner. Blackburn are getting great joy down their right through Alebiosu and Morishita, with the latter winning them a corner as Toti is forced to head behind from a cross. Cantwell’s delivery to the far post is headed away.

We have the first goal of the season and it’s the returning Marshall Munetsi who gets it.

A cool finish from the midfielder after a bit of a drab start from the home side.

That will please the new Wolves boss. Such a simple move but the home side ripped Blackburn wide open with two passes.

Work to do for the visitors now who had probably started the better of the two teams before the opener.

Wolves fans make their feelings about VAR known following the goal. No VAR in the Championship of course but no VAR was needed for that anyway. A perfectly good goal.

Mane cuts inside from the left onto his preferred right foot and curls a dangerous ball into the box that is punched away by Toth in the Blackburn goal. 18-year-old Mane was one of very few bright spots for Wolves last season and in many ways it is a surprise that no Premier League teams have lured him back to the top flight quite yet. That could though still happen before the deadline.

The first goal of the Championship season comes against the run of play. It is a clinical, ruthless goal that comes from an incisive pass and clinical finish. The pass is fed through by F Lopez to pick out the run of Munetsi, who is cool, calm and collected as he finishes past Toth. Blackburn had been the better side up until that point but Wolves take the lead at Molineux.

"A vibrant Molineux rejoices!" 🎉Marshall Munetsi cooly slots home for Wolves to give them the lead on the opening night of the Championship season 🥶 pic.twitter.com/tVHdbNv3Hq

A shot on target for Blackburn but an easy save in the end. Alebiosu, who has looked good in these early stages, drives down Blackburn’s right before cutting it back to Morishita on the edge of the box. Morishita takes one touch before shooting but his effort is tame and straight at Bentley.

Blackburn have definitely been the better side in these early exchanges, dominating possession and looking a threat going forward.

Blackburn may be heavy underdogs tonight but they have settled down well away at one of the favourites to get promoted. Tony Mowbray may well be seeing this as a good time to play Wolves away.

Alebiosu shows quick feet down Blackburn’s right and clips a cross to the back post, where Afolayan meets it but his header is just off target.

Safe to say the doom and gloom of last season appears to have lifted at Molineux. The home fans in fine voice early on here.

By contrast, Kieran Trippier’s first touch of the season is greeted by loud boos by the travelling Blackburn supporters.

In fact, every Trippier touch is greeted by a chorus of boos. Will they keep that up all game?

They’ve certainly not forgotten his Burnley connection.

New managers and new signings galore. This should be a fascinating spectacle.

He may not be in the starting XI tonight but Jimenez is being serenaded by the home fans on his return to Wolves after a few years away at Fulham. Jimenez and his wife have paid for 5,000 scarves for the Wolves fans tonight.

Blackburn boss Tony Mowbray did say ahead of the game that Wolves have not been used to winning games over the last 12 months so can the visitors take advantage of that tonight? Blackburn are underdogs tonight and not too much is expected of them this season so surely they have nothing to lose this evening?

Due to his Burnley ties, new Wolves defender Trippier is booed by the travelling Blackburn fans. On the other side of defence for Wolves is Moller Wolfe, who started for Norway against England in the World Cup quarter-finals in Miami.

After Jeff Beck’s Hi Ho Silver Lining rings around the stadium and tributes paid to former Wolves goalkeeper Phil Parkes, we are under way at Molineux. The 2026/27 Championship season is officially under way.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off on opening night in the Championship.

When Wolverhampton Wanderers last attacked the Championship under a Portuguese manager new to English football, it proved a vintage season.

Molineux was under the spell of Nuno Espírito Santo in that 2017-18 campaign, and the big question is whether César Peixoto can lead a repeat nearly a decade later.

Peixoto was a surprise appointment in June, replacing Rob Edwards, and he has been entrusted with the mission of returning Wolves to the Premier League at the first time of asking.

“I have changed some things with set-pieces and some things in other moments of the game because I want the team to be organised and understand all the different moments within a match. During pre-season we have scored some goals from high pressing, but we will not be able to press high in every moment of every game. The players have to understand the game and recognise what each moment requires. It is important that we work as a team. When we can press high, we’ll press high. When we need to defend in a mid-block, we will stay organised. When the opposition pushes us deeper, which will sometimes happen, we have to be organised there as well.

“There are a lot of crosses in the Championship, for example, so the team needs to understand what to do in those situations. We want to play our football, be offensive and react strongly when we lose the ball, but we also need to understand the different moments of the game. I think we are at a good level to attack the Championship.”

Our experts have been having their say ahead of the new Championship season. A number of them believe Wolves will be promoted, including John Percy:

It is difficult to look beyond West Ham. Nuno Espírito Santo romped to the Championship title with Wolves in 2018 and remains a shrewd operator (along with his No 2 Rui Pedro Silva), while convincing Jarrod Bowen to stay is significant. I am going to go for Wolves and Middlesbrough as the other two promoted clubs.
